How to make cookies, step by step

Once you decide what type of cookie you’re making (learn about some of the most common ones here), it’s time to put the dough together. First thing’s first: read through the entire recipe and follow it exactly as it’s written, as obvious as that sounds, says Penny Stankiewicz, a chef-instructor of pastry and baking arts at the Institute of Culinary Education. Don’t substitute ingredients — if you do, your cookies won’t taste or have the same texture as the recipe intended.

There’s one exception to the rule: You can play with a recipe’s flavors and mix-ins. “As long as you don’t mess with the structural ingredients of the recipe, like flour, butter and sugar, you’re not going to wreck its integrity,” says Stankiewicz. “For example, you can change how much vanilla extract you add, sprinkle cinnamon into your dough or use two types of chocolate chips instead of one.”
Below are tools experts recommend using while making cookie dough.

You can measure ingredients by volume or by weight. Measuring by volume involves using liquid and dry measuring cups, while measuring by weight involves using a kitchen scale. Arlyn Osborne, a recipe developer, food writer and the author of “Sugarcane,” recommends measuring ingredients by weight since it’s more precise and helps ensure that cookies are consistent every time you make them.
Etekcity Digital Kitchen Scale

As Osborne recommends, I measure by weight while baking cookies using a digital kitchen scale like this one. I sit the scale on my counter, put a small bowl on top, zero the scale and weigh out each ingredient before adding it to my main mixing bowl. Etekcity’s scale measures liquids and solids in five units, which you can alternate between using a dedicated button. It runs on (and comes with) two AA batteries and automatically turns off after two minutes of inactivity. The scale, which has an 11-pound maximum capacity, is slim enough to put in most kitchen drawers.
Joseph Joseph Nest Measuring Cup Set

If you prefer measuring by volume, you’ll need dry measuring cups for ingredients like flour, sugar and baking powder. These come in an eight-piece set that measures from one teaspoon to one cup, and they nest into each other to save storage space. Their handles also snap together, keeping them connected in your drawer. The measuring cups are dishwasher safe.
Pyrex Essentials Glass Measuring Cups

To prevent measurement inaccuracies, stick to measuring dry ingredients with dry measuring cups, like the Joseph Joseph ones above, and wet ingredients with liquid measuring cups, like these from Pyrex. You get three glass measuring cups in the set with capacities of 1, 2 and 4 cups. They have easily readable measurement markers in ounces and milliliters on the sides, sturdy handles and pour spouts. The cups are safe to put in the dishwasher, freezer, microwave and preheated oven.

The majority of cookies home bakers make involve the creaming method, which means the first step in the recipe is to cream room temperature butter and sugar together, says Stankiewicz. Using a stand mixer with the paddle attachment is the easiest way to do so. Experts also recommend keeping a flexible silicone spatula on hand to periodically scrape the sides of the bowl. You can use a hand mixer or spoon to cream butter and sugar for cookies, but it’s not as efficient.
KitchenAid Artisan 5-Qt. Tilt Head Stand Mixer

Any brand’s stand mixer will do, but Stankiewicz prefers KitchenAid’s, and I’m loyal to mine, too. It’s one of the most reliable appliances I own and the workhorse of my kitchen, especially while baking. The mixer’s 5-quart, dishwasher-safe, stainless steel bowl can hold enough dough to make up to nine dozen cookies — that’s 108 total. You can adjust the mixer’s speed across 10 levels, and the tilt-head design gives you lots of room to add ingredients. The mixer comes with three attachments: a coated flat beater (which you’ll use to cream butter and sugar together for cookies), a wire whip (perfect for homemade frosting to decorate cookies) and a dough hook. You also get a pouring shield to prevent messes while adding ingredients when the mixer is on.
GIR Ultimate Spatula

I use this spatula to scrape the sides of my bowl while making cookies. It’s 11 inches long, giving me plenty of room on the handle to maintain a sturdy grip, and it has a flexible head that bends around curves and gets into corners. The silicone tool is heat-resistant up to 425 degrees Fahrenheit, so I can dip it into hot melted chocolate and butter, and it’s dishwasher safe.

Mixing bowls are available in materials like glass, ceramic and metal, but it ultimately doesn’t matter when it comes to making cookies, says Elizabeth Barbone, a recipe developer and cookbook author who runs the sites Cook Fast, Eat Well and Gluten-Free Baking. What does matter is the mixing bowl’s size. Ingredients spill out of bowls that are too small while you’re stirring, and while there’s no such thing as a bowl that’s too big while you’re hand-mixing, there is if you’re using a stand mixer. Mixing bowls that are too big may prevent the mixer’s paddle from reaching its sides, smearing ingredients into a paste along the bottom of the bowl instead of whipping it until fluffy, says Barbone.
Cuisinart Mixing Bowl Set

I like having mixing bowls in multiple sizes available to me so I can pick the right one for how much cookie dough I’m making. I gravitate toward metal ones since they’re the most durable. This  Cuisinart set checks all my boxes. It comes with 1.5-, 3- and 5-quart mixing bowls, each of which are made from stainless steel and come with matching lids — that means I can make cookie dough, put a lid on the bowl and put it in the refrigerator to chill. The bowls nest into each other for compact storage.
Each type of cookie has a signature shape (learn more about here), which you achieve using specific tools. Below, I listed what you need to form a few popular ones.

Cookie scoops help you create balls of dough for drop cookies that are the exact same size, ensuring that the batch bakes evenly, says Barbone. She prefers cookie scoops with trigger handles since they quickly release balls of dough, which makes shaping drop cookies fast and efficient.

Cookie scoops come in a variety of sizes, which you’ll see listed as a number that corresponds to the number of scoops per quart of dough. For example, a #40 scoop gives you about 40 scoops per quart and a #10 scoop gives you about 10 scoops per quart — this means the #10 scoop is larger than the #40 scoop. There’s no standard scoop size you should look for, but #40 is common for cookies, says Barbone. If you make cookies often, consider buying a large, medium and small scoop so all your bases are covered.
Gorilla Grip #40 Cookie Scoop

This dishwasher-safe #40 cookie scoop is as basic as they come. It picks up about 2 tablespoons of dough to make cookies that are about 3 inches wide. The scoop has a trigger handle, as Barbone recommends, that’s covered in soft rubber to keep your hand comfortable while gripping it.  If you want a scoop to make smaller or bigger cookies, Gorilla Grip makes options that pick up 2 teaspoons, 1 tablespoon and 3 tablespoons of dough, too.

You don’t technically need to buy a rolling pin since you can use household objects as alternatives, like wine bottles and canned foods. But a rolling pin gives you more even results while making cutout cookies, so if you plan on baking often, it’s nice to have.
J.K. Adams French Tapered Rolling Pin

Osborne prefers using a French tapered rolling pin, like this one, which is shaped like a baton — it’s wider in the middle and narrower at the ends. She says it’s easy to maneuver and gives you lots of surface area to place your hands while going over the dough. J.K. Adams’ lightweight rolling pin is made from warp-resistant hardwood and it has a textured surface that successfully holds onto flour, so you only need a light dusting to prevent dough from sticking. It’s 20.5 inches long and comes in 1.5-inch and 1.75-inch thicknesses. The brand recommends hand-washing it.

Cookie cutters come in hundreds of shapes: circles, hearts, squares, gingerbread men, menorahs, animals, numbers, letters, symbols… you name it, there’s a cookie cutter for it. Some companies even let you create custom cookie cutters, which is a great option for themed events. There’s options made from plastic and metal, either of which will do, but each material has strengths and weaknesses.

Metal cookie cutters give cookies clean, crisp edges and they’re easy to clean since you can put them in the dishwasher, says Barbone. But they’re sharper compared to plastic cutters, so they’re not kid-friendly. Metal cookie cutters are also quite durable, says Stankiewicz. If you care for them properly, they can last for decades. In fact, Stankiewicz says her family’s copper cookie cutters have been passed down for generations.Plastic cookie cutters are duller compared to metal options. This makes them suitable for kids, but they can give cookies messy, smushed edges, says Barbone. Even if the plastic cookie cutters you buy say they’re dishwasher safe, it’s best to hand-wash them, says Stankiewicz — heat from the dishwasher can cause them to melt or become misshapen.

Metal cookie cutters give cookies clean, crisp edges and they’re easy to clean since you can put them in the dishwasher, says Barbone. But they’re sharper compared to plastic cutters, so they’re not kid-friendly. Metal cookie cutters are also quite durable, says Stankiewicz. If you care for them properly, they can last for decades. In fact, Stankiewicz says her family’s copper cookie cutters have been passed down for generations.

Plastic cookie cutters are duller compared to metal options. This makes them suitable for kids, but they can give cookies messy, smushed edges, says Barbone. Even if the plastic cookie cutters you buy say they’re dishwasher safe, it’s best to hand-wash them, says Stankiewicz — heat from the dishwasher can cause them to melt or become misshapen.
Ann Clark 11-Piece Christmas Cookie Cutters Set

Ann Clark makes cookie cutters for almost every occasion, and you can buy many of them individually as well as in sets like this Christmas-themed one. It comes with 11 cookie cutters in shapes like a snowflake, gingerbread man, mitter, candy cane and angel. The cutters are made from steel, which quickly cuts through dough and leaves behind sharp edges. The upper edge is rolled to protect your hand while gripping them, and the brand recommends hand-washing them.

A cookie press, which you use to make spritz cookies, is a cylindrical tool with a plunger on one end and interchangeable discs on the other. Each disc has cutouts on it, creating different shapes. You load dough into the body of the press and use the plunger to push it through the disc’s holes, resulting in perfectly shaped cookies. You move the press’ head along the sheet pan and push out one cookie at a time.

Barbone recommends buying a cookie press that comes with metal discs, which cleanly release dough so each cookie’s shape is clearly defined. Avoid plastic cookie presses: They’re more prone to getting clogged and breaking, she says.
OXO Good Grips 14-Piece Cookie Press Set

I’ve tested a few cookie presses, and overall, I find OXO’s the easiest to fill, use, swap discs and clean. It comes apart, letting you add dough to the barrel and put one of the 12 included stainless steel discs on the end. Then, you screw everything back together, stand the press up on a sheet pan and press down on the lever. A neatly shaped cookie comes out, and you repeat the process until your dough is gone. Since the barrel is clear, you can see exactly how much dough you have left, and the 12 discs come in a storage case to prevent you from losing any. The barrel, bottom ring and discs are dishwasher-safe, but the top and plunger are hand-wash only.

After rolling dough into logs while making slice-and-bake cookies, you wrap each one in plastic cling wrap and put them in the refrigerator for a few hours or overnight. The plastic wrap keeps the dough fresh while it’s chilling and keeps odors and moisture out. If you’re looking for a plastic wrap alternative, reusable beeswax wrap is a great option, and some brands make silicone tools to help you size, shape and store slice-and-bake dough.
OXO Good Grips Slice & Bake Cookie Helper

Slice-and-bake cookies are one of my go-to bakes, so it’s no wonder why OXO’s dishwasher-safe Good Grips Slice & Bake Cookie Helper is one of my favorite reusable tools. It comes with two flexible silicone mats, which you use to roll dough into a log like you would with plastic wrap, and there’s a clasp that keeps it together. The mat also has built-in measurement guides on it, which get imprinted on the log and give you marks to follow while slicing. You cover each open end of the log with the included caps before putting it in the refrigerator or freezer to cool. After a few hours or so, you unroll the silicone mats, put the logs on a cutting board and use the measurement guides to cut 1.5-inch, 1.75-inch or 2-inch slices.

Putting cookies in the oven is often the most nerve-wracking step for home bakers — no one wants to put effort into perfecting dough and end up with a burnt final product. To ensure cookies come out golden brown and ready to sink your teeth into, use the below expert-recommended tools.

Even when you set your oven to a specific temperature, it probably doesn’t warm up to exactly where you want it, unless it was recently calibrated, says Stankiewicz. This means your baked goods are likely cooking at a slightly lower or higher temperature than you’re anticipating, which impacts cooking time. To confirm that your oven reaches the right temperature before adding your cookies, Stankiewicz recommends buying an oven thermometer. It hooks onto the oven’s racks and reads its internal temperature, which you can monitor while your oven is preheating to adjust its settings accordingly.
Rubbermaid Oven Monitoring Thermometer

Find out how warm your oven actually is before putting cookies inside using Rubbermaid’s battery-free thermometer — it helps you monitor the temperature throughout the baking process, too. It hooks onto the rack in your oven and reads temperatures between 60 and 580 degrees Fahrenheit.

Experts recommend keeping a few half-sheet pans in your kitchen at all times because they’re so versatile. You can use them to bake and cook sweet and savory foods, plus they last for years if cared for properly.

For cookies specifically, it’s best to use rimmed sheet pans. “I never use a sheet pan without a rim because there’s always a chance something could slide off the edge,” says Barbone. This is especially the case with cookies. Recipes often tell you to rotate the sheet pan halfway through to ensure all of the cookies bake evenly, and if your sheet pan doesn’t have a rim, the cookies may slide off during this process.

Additionally, pay attention to the color of your sheet pan. Darker sheet pans tend to conduct more heat, which means the bottoms of your cookies will bake faster than the tops, says Stankiewicz. This is often why people end up with cookies that are burnt on the bottom but still raw on top. Use a lighter colored sheet pan to avoid this issue, says Stankiewicz.
Great Jones Holy Sheet Pan

I was originally drawn to Great Jones’ Holy Sheet Pan because it’s so good looking, and I’m happy to report that it works just as well. The half-sheet pan has a rim around its perimeter, preventing my cookies from sliding off, and it comes in a handful of colors, which aren’t super dark to encourage even browning. The pan is made from aluminized steel with a nonstick coating, and while it’s dishwasher-friendly, the brand recommends hand-washing it. You can put it in ovens up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. In addition to baking cookies on this sheet pan, I decorate, serve and display them on it.

Parchment paper and silicone baking mats serve the same purpose and are essentially interchangeable when it comes to baking cookies. They line your sheet pan, provide a nonstick surface to bake on and make cleanup a breeze. You can also line your pan with tin foil, but since the material conducts heat, it tends to make the bottoms of your cookies darker and speed up baking time — try to avoid it if you can, says Sarah House, the food innovation chef and recipe and development lead at Bob’s Red Mill.

Beyond one being disposable and the other being reusable, the main difference between parchment paper and silicone baking mats is how much cookies grip onto them. Silicone baking mats are so nonstick that cookies don’t have much to grasp onto, which might cause them to spread too much while baking, says Barbone. Parchment paper is still nonstick, but cookies can grip to it more, reducing spread. Barbone opts for parchment paper instead of silicone baking mats for cookies, but it’s ultimately a personal preference.
Baker’s Signature Parchment Paper Sheets

Stankiewicz recommends buying parchment paper in sheets rather than rolls. Rolled parchment paper tends to curl in on itself, making it challenging to cut to your desired size. Sheets of flat parchment paper, on the other hand, and won’t curl, so cutting it is easy, although doing so may not be necessary if you buy sheets that are the same size as your sheet pans.

Baker’s Signature’s Parchment Paper Sheets come in various sizes and shapes to match different types of pans. They’re made from natural wood pulp with a nonstick coating, are oven-safe up to 425 degrees Fahrenheit and won’t curl, stick or burn, according to the brand.

Always keep track of how long cookies have been in the oven relative to the estimated bake time detailed by your recipe. You can use a mechanical or digital timer, or devices like your phone or watch.

Remember that a recipe’s estimated bake time is just a guideline, says Stankiewicz. Factors like the type of oven you’re using, whether you preheated it and how many trays of cookies are baking at once can impact baking time. Because of this, one of the best ways to determine cookie doneness is by using your nose. “Once you start smelling the cookies, start checking on them,” says Stankiewicz. From there, pay attention to the cookies’ color and texture. Fully baked cookies are usually golden brown and have a matte rather than glossy appearance, so once you see those signs and smell them, pull them out of the oven.
TempPro TM01 Kitchen Timer

You can set a timer on your phone, tablet, smartwatch or smart home devices to monitor cookie baking, but there’s something about using a standard kitchen timer that I like better — perhaps I just find it more reliable since it has one job. TempPro’s timer lets you count up or down, and when time runs out, an alarm sounds. The screen is backlit so you can see it if you’re in a darker kitchen, and you can prop the timer up on a flat surface using the built-in stand or, because it has a magnetic back, stick it on a refrigerator or microwave.

When you take your cookies out of the oven, let them cool on the sheet pan for five to 10 minutes before gently moving them to a cooling rack with a spatula, says House. If you leave cookies on a hot pan, they’ll continue baking and can become overdone. But placing cookies on a cooling rack allows air to circulate around them, cooling them quickly and preventing extra baking.
Ultra Cuisine Stainless Steel Baking & Cooling Rack

I always end up making more cookies than I plan on, so one cooling rack doesn’t cut it — this pack of two makes sure I always have a backup. The dishwasher-safe racks are around the same size as half-sheet pans, made from stainless steel and oven-safe up to 575 degrees Fahrenheit.
Fox Run Stainless Steel Cookie and Brownie Spatula

Transfer cookies from the hot pan, to the cooling rack and to a plate or serving dish with this spatula. Its stainless steel head has a beveled edge, so it easily slides under cookies, and its wood handle helps you keep a steady grip while moving your baked goods.

Once the cookies are cool, decorate them however you’d like, although it’s not a required step — they’re delicious straight out of the oven. A few ideas: you can dust your cookies with powdered sugar, make a glaze or frosting or top them with sprinkles.
Ateco 1385 Offset Spatula

An offset spatula like this one is helpful while spreading glaze and frosting over cookies. I keep a bunch of them in my kitchen so I don’t have to constantly clean one if I’m using frostings and glazes in different colors or flavors. A 4.5-inch spatula is the ideal size for cookies, in my experience — anything bigger overpowers the cookie and doesn’t give you enough control. This one has a tapered stainless steel blade and a wood handle, and the brand recommends hand-washing it.
Wilton Beginner Buttercream Decorating Set

If you want to get fancy, a set of piping tips and bags can help you create detailed designs on your cookies, says House. This set comes with 10 stainless steel decorating tips, including round, star, petal and leaf options, and 10 frosting bags. The tips are technically top-rack dishwasher-safe, but the brand recommends hand-washing them. If you’re new to piping designs, I highly recommend watching YouTube tutorials or those on social media — that’s how I learned the basics, and I still use them now when I want to learn something new.

As long as you bake cookies all the way through, the experts I talked to say most batches have a week-long shelf life. Store them in a container with a tightly sealed lid to keep air, odors and moisture out, and stack them with parchment paper between each layer so they don’t stick together.

If you need to store fully baked cookies beyond a week, Barbone recommends freezing them. The best way to do so is by laying the cookies out on a sheet pan or plate and putting them in the freezer. Once they’re frozen, transfer them to an airtight container or a tightly sealed bag. Frozen cookies keep well for at least three to five months, says Osborne.
Pyrex Simple Store Glass Food Storage Container

In my experience, Pyrex’s 11-cup glass container is the ideal shape, depth and size for storing a dozen or so cookies in two or three layers, separated by parchment paper. The lid creates a tight seal around the opening, keeping air, moisture and odors out so your cookies stay fresh. The container is freezer-safe if you want to keep frozen cookies inside it, and it’s dishwasher-safe.
Stasher Stand-Up Mega Premium Reusable Silicone Bag

I don’t have room in my freezer for a large container like Pyrex’s, so I store frozen cookies (and cookie dough balls) in Stasher’s freezer-safe reusable silicone bags. I particularly like the Stand-Up Mega because it has a flat base — as its name implies, it stands up by itself, making filling it easy. You pinch the bag’s seal closed to keep air, moisture and odors out, and you can write on it in dry-erase marker to label what type of cookies are inside, as well as when you froze them. Stasher bags are dishwasher safe.
What are the most popular types of cookies?

Drop cookies: As the name implies, you make drop cookies by dropping balls of dough onto a sheet pan. The dough spreads in the oven, giving the cookies a round shape once baked — think typical chocolate chip cookies, for example. Drop cookies are the easiest cookies to make.Cut out cookies: The star of any holiday cookie box, cut out cookies are made by rolling out dough and using cookie cutters to create shapes. They’re also a great option for beginner bakers. People traditionally make cut out cookies from sugar or gingerbread cookie dough, but the flavor possibilities are endless. Slice-and-bake cookies: To make slice-and-bake cookies, you roll dough into logs and refrigerate them. Once the dough is chilled, you slice the logs into rounds and bake them on a cookie sheet. Slice-and-bake cookies are shortbread cookies, meaning they’re buttery and have a crumbly texture. They’re pretty straightforward to make.Spritz cookies: You make spritz cookies with a cookie press, a tool that pushes dough through a patterned disc. The dough is very soft, which makes it easy to force through the press. Once they bake, spritz cookies have a lighter texture compared to cut out cookies, says Barbone. Using a cookie press can be tricky, so experts recommend mastering more beginner-friendly bakes first, like drop, cut out and slice-and-bake cookies.

People traditionally make cut out cookies from sugar or gingerbread cookie dough, but the flavor possibilities are endless.

Once they bake, spritz cookies have a lighter texture compared to cut out cookies, says Barbone. Using a cookie press can be tricky, so experts recommend mastering more beginner-friendly bakes first, like drop, cut out and slice-and-bake cookies.
Experts’ top cookie baking tips
Throughout their years of baking cookies, the experts I talked to have seen and experienced their fair share of mistakes. Below are their tips for avoiding common issues.

Cookie dough easily sticks to your rolling pin and countertop. To prevent this, people often sprinkle flour on the dough and surface its resting on, but doing so adds flour to the dough and too much can dry it out. Instead, Stankiewicz recommends rolling out the dough between two pieces of parchment paper to prevent sticking.If you’re measuring dry ingredients by volume, spoon them into measuring cups until they dome over the top. Then scrape a knife along the top of the measuring cups to level them off, says Osborne. This helps you avoid adding excess ingredients to your dough.The bottoms of cookies can burn for a number of reasons, but if you notice it happening every time you use a specific sheet pan, odds are the pan is too thin. Thin sheet pans transfer too much heat to cookies’ bases, causing them to bake faster than the rest of the treat and get darker at the bottom. Instead of buying a new set of pans, consider stacking two on top of each other, says Osborne. Doing so adds an extra layer of protection for the cookies’ bases since the two pans absorb double the amount of heat.To keep cookies soft, add a piece of white bread to the container you’re storing them in. The bread releases moisture inside the container, which the cookies slowly absorb so they don’t dry out. Replace the piece of bread every two days.If drop cookies lose their round shape in the oven, it’s fixable. Cookies are soft and moldable when they’re hot, so you can adjust them slightly, turning them back into a perfect circle. Take a circular cookie cutter or cup that fits over your cookies and gently swirl it around each one immediately after removing the pan from the oven, says Stankiewicz.

Cookie dough easily sticks to your rolling pin and countertop. To prevent this, people often sprinkle flour on the dough and surface its resting on, but doing so adds flour to the dough and too much can dry it out. Instead, Stankiewicz recommends rolling out the dough between two pieces of parchment paper to prevent sticking.

If you’re measuring dry ingredients by volume, spoon them into measuring cups until they dome over the top. Then scrape a knife along the top of the measuring cups to level them off, says Osborne. This helps you avoid adding excess ingredients to your dough.

The bottoms of cookies can burn for a number of reasons, but if you notice it happening every time you use a specific sheet pan, odds are the pan is too thin. Thin sheet pans transfer too much heat to cookies’ bases, causing them to bake faster than the rest of the treat and get darker at the bottom. Instead of buying a new set of pans, consider stacking two on top of each other, says Osborne. Doing so adds an extra layer of protection for the cookies’ bases since the two pans absorb double the amount of heat.

To keep cookies soft, add a piece of white bread to the container you’re storing them in. The bread releases moisture inside the container, which the cookies slowly absorb so they don’t dry out. Replace the piece of bread every two days.

If drop cookies lose their round shape in the oven, it’s fixable. Cookies are soft and moldable when they’re hot, so you can adjust them slightly, turning them back into a perfect circle. Take a circular cookie cutter or cup that fits over your cookies and gently swirl it around each one immediately after removing the pan from the oven, says Stankiewicz.
Frequently asked questions

Most cookie dough benefits from chilling in the refrigerator before you bake it, says Stankiewicz. Cold dough keeps its shape better and spreads less in the oven compared to warm or room temperature dough. But any cookie that you prefer to be thin and crispy can do without chilling time, says House.

To chill dough, place it in the refrigerator for at least an hour or up to 24 hours prior to baking. Make sure you cover it in plastic wrap so it doesn’t take on other flavors or fall victim to spills, says House.
Yes, you can freeze most types of cookie dough. In fact, experts recommend doing so. “The freezer is your friend,” says Stankiewicz.

To freeze cookie dough, make a batch of it, shape it, place it on a sheet pan and pop it in the freezer. Once fully frozen, transfer the dough to an air-tight container or bag and leave it in the freezer. Stankiewicz recommends putting a piece of plastic cling wrap underneath your container’s lid to keep air out.

When you’re ready to make a few cookies, place the frozen dough on a lined sheet pan and place it in a preheated oven. You don’t need to defrost the dough before baking it, but be aware that the cookies may take an additional minute or two to cook through, so adjust your baking time, says Stankiewicz.

Oven placement matters while baking cookies, says Stankiewicz. It’s usually best to place the pan on the middle rack in your oven, which is considered the sweet spot. The middle rack circulates air around the entire pan, evenly baking the cookies. Your recipe will also likely tell you to rotate the pan halfway through baking, which helps the cookies bake evenly, says Stankiewicz.

Additionally, Osborne doesn’t recommend baking two trays of cookies at a time. Odds are, both trays won’t be able to fit on the middle rack, subjecting one to less than optimal oven conditions. If you absolutely have to bake two trays of cookies at once, Osborne recommends putting one pan on the oven’s center rack and one of the oven’s topmost rack. Swap and rotate them halfway through baking.

Unless your recipe specifically calls for melted butter, softened room temperature is best for baking cookies. “The temperature of the fat, which is usually butter, is key to a low-stress cookie dough making experience,” says House. “Too soft will make a loose batter that spreads, too cold will just be messy and frustrating. Use butter that you can make an indentation in with just the slightest bit of pressure.”
Meet our baking experts

At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest.

Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who’s written about kitchen tools for over six years, including articles about pie baking tools, Dutch ovens, nonstick cookware and plastic-free cutting boards. I’ve also been an avid baker for over a decade. To write this article, I interviewed four professional bakers about their favorite cookie baking tools and tips. I curated a list of their recommendations, and I also added products that I swear by after testing them.

title: 23+ gifts the coffee lovers in your life will be buzzing about beyond the holidays
summary: The best gifts to buy coffee lovers include beans, mugs, brewers and brewing accessories. Here are our top picks, hand-picked by coffee lovers themselves.
story: I wake up, go to sleep and spend many hours in between thinking about my next cup of coffee, so it’s not an exaggeration to call myself the expert when it comes to finding the best gifts for coffee lovers (at least at NBC Selected). Sure, you can always rely on the standard nice bag of beans or  oversized mug, but there’s so much more out there. Coffee-flavored lip balms, delectable syrups, adorable espresso cups, sleek brewers that double as decor, chocolate-covered beans — I could go on and on.

To help you fuel your recipient’s obsession this holiday season, I curated a list of the best gifts for coffee lovers below. I included my favorite products, as well as ones tested and loved by our team of shopping experts. I’ll continue to update this article throughout the holiday season in case you need even more inspiration.

The best gifts for coffee lovers overall
Door County Coffee 12 Days of Coffee

The coffee lover in your life can count down to whatever holiday they celebrate with this 12-day Advent calendar. There’s a bag of ground coffee behind each door, which they can use to brew a full pot with 40 ounces of water. The coffees are seasonally flavored — options include Candy Cane, Espresso Martini, Mistletoe Mocha, White Chocolate Cranberry and Cinnamon Hazelnut.
Door County Coffee also makes a 24-day coffee advent calendar with ground beans and a 12-day coffee calendar with single-serve coffee pods.
Bialetti Mini Express Lichtenstein

Bialetti’s stovetop espresso maker makes two shots at a time, so your favorite coffee lover can either get extra caffeinated or make a drink for themselves and a guest once they unwrap it. Plus, it’s beautifully designed, so they can keep it out as a piece of decor. The Bialetti Mini Express Lichtenstein comes with two espresso cups that fit perfectly underneath each spout, and you can choose from styles like Pop Art, Kandinsky, Magritte and Modern.
Ember Mug 3

No one likes rushing to drink their coffee before it gets cold, or microwaving it if they forget about it. Ember’s self-heating mug, which comes highly recommended by NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio, prevents both of those situations, allowing your giftee to take their time while enjoying their favorite beverage. They can use the brand’s app or the buttons on the mug to set their preferred temperature up to 145 degrees Fahrenheit.

The dishwasher-safe mug keeps drinks hot for up to three hours in cordless mode with the lid, or all day when resting on the included charging coaster. The Ember Mug 3 comes in 10-ounce, 14-ounce and 16-ounce sizes.
Jellycat Amuseable Espresso Cup

Simply seeing a Jellycat makes most people smile — add the fact that it’s shaped like an espresso cup and the coffee connoisseur in your life will adore it even more. The tiny 2-inch plushie is great decor at the office or at home, and it might even kickstart your giftee’s Jellycat collection.
Aieve Espresso Cooling Balls

We all have that one person in our lives who only drinks iced lattes. If that sounds like someone you’re buying a gift for, look no further than this espresso cooling ball. It sits on a cup underneath a machine’s spout, and as the espresso brews, it passes over the ball before dripping into the cup. The ball, which your giftee has to freeze for at least four hours beforehand, instantly lowers the espresso’s temperature by 80 to 100 degrees and removes bitter notes, according to the brand. That means the shot is the perfect temperature to immediately add to a cup with ice and milk — no more waiting around for it to cool down.

“The cooling ball definitely makes espresso shots taste better than a normal brew and speeds up the whole process,” says NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack, who uses it at home every day. We recommend using the cooling balls (this comes as a set of two) as a secret Santa or white elephant gift, making them a stocking stuffer or gifting them alongside beans or espresso cups (like the Yeti ones below).
Beans, concentrates and syrups
Atlas Coffee Club Gourmet Coffee Sampler Gift Set

Introduce your loved one to coffees from around the world with Atlas Coffee Club’s sampler set. It comes with eight 1.8-ounce bags of whole bean or ground coffee (you pick one before checking out), which brews about four cups. They’ll try blends from Costa Rica, Kenya, India, Peru and other countries, and learn about each one using the included tasting note cards and origin story postcards. Everything comes packed inside a box, so you can ship it directly to your recipient or put a bow on it and give it to them in person.
Jot Ultra Coffee Concentrate Trio

No coffee machine? No problem. By following the ratios on the bottles, your loved one can use Jot’s coffee concentrates to make hot coffee, iced coffee and espresso-based drinks like lattes. This trio comes with three types of Jot coffee concentrate: original, vanilla and dark (an extra bold variety). I’ve tried them all and am impressed by how smooth and flavorful they are regardless of what drink I use them for. Each bottle makes 14 servings.
Cometeer Curated Bundle

Your giftee can also use Cometeer’s frozen coffee concentrate pods to make hot, iced and espresso-based beverages without a brewer (there’s directions on the box that walk them through exactly how). The brand works with popular roasters across the country to bring their blends to customers, and this bundle lets your loved one try a handful of them. It’s curated by Cometeer’s team the week you buy it to ensure your giftee gets the freshest pods possible.

They’ll receive five sleeves of coffee with eight capsules in each one, letting them make 40 cups total. You can choose from six types of bundles: mixed roast, medium roast, light roast, dark roast, decaf and half-caff.
Proper Vanilla Syrup

You’ll instantly upgrade your giftee’s coffee game by getting them Proper’s syrups, which come in flavors like vanilla, salted caramel, simple, pumpkin spice and pistachio. They come in glass bottles that are good looking enough to be displayed on your giftee’s coffee bar, and Cusack says they’re some of the best ones she’s tasted.

“One of my pet peeves is when the syrup sinks to the bottom of my drink, but I haven’t found that with Proper syrups — they blend in quickly, so I’m not finishing my coffee with a gulp of straight syrup,” she says. “The flavors are subtle, not too overpowering or too sweet and make a great addition to my morning iced lattes. I’ve even used the syrups in other drinks, like dirty sodas and cocktails — my secret ingredient for the perfect at-home espresso martini is Proper’s vanilla syrup.”
Brewers
Breville Bambino Espresso Machine

This itty-bitty espresso machine won’t take up much space on your giftee’s countertop while they fulfill their at-home barista dreams. It’s simple to operate with very few buttons, and it quickly heats up to make single or double shots. The machine also has an automatic steam wand, and your loved one can adjust the milk temperature and texture settings to their liking.
They get all the accessories they need with the Breville Bambino, including filter baskets, a portafilter, a milk jug, a tamper and a steam wand cleaning tool, as well as two bags of coffee.
Chemex Pour-Over Glass Coffee Maker Classic Series

“My husband is a huge pour-over coffee fan, so I got him the Chemex as a gift and it’s become a staple in my house,” says Godio. The top of the Chemex is cone-shaped, so your loved one adds a disposable filter and their favorite grounds, pours hot water over them, and watches as coffee drips into the bottom. “The carafe is insulated to keep the coffee hot, and the wood collar and leather tie serve as a handle, so I don’t burn my hand when I pour it into a mug,” says Godio.
Your giftee can take the “handle” off and the carafe is dishwasher-safe for easy cleanup. The Chemex comes in 3-cup, 6-cup, 8-cup and 10-cup sizes.
Wacaco Minipresso GR Portable Espresso Machine

The traveler or outdoor enthusiast in your life won’t have to settle for mediocre coffee on the go once you buy them Wacaco’s portable machine, which NBC Selected video editor Josh Rios calls a “pocket barista that makes a solid cut of espresso.” Your giftee can simply add ground beans and hot water to the lightweight, compact gadget, and press down on a button to brew manually — it’s battery-free and doesn’t need to be charged. Its cap doubles as a cup, too.
Moccamaster by Technivorm KBGV Select Coffee Maker

“Yes, the Moccamaster is expensive for a drip coffee maker, but it’s one of my favorite things I own,” says Godio. The caffeine-obsessed person in your life will feel the same once they set it up, and since it has such a sleek look, it will become a focal point in their kitchen. “The flavor of the coffee is so much better than any other drip coffee maker I’ve tried, and I can keep the glass carafe on the hot plate so my coffee stays warm for over an hour.”
The Moccamaster can make up to 10 cups of coffee in four to six minutes, and your giftee can control the holding temperature of the hot plate post-brewing.
Mugs and brewing accessories
Exception Lab Ceramic Greek Coffee Cup

New York City’s iconic Greek Coffee Cup is one of my favorite keepsakes to give friends and family who live in the area, moved away or love visiting. It’s made from ceramic, so it’s dishwasher- and microwave-safe, and it holds about 10 ounces of coffee. Your loved one can drink from it, but it’s also a cute tchotchke to display at home or put pens in on a desk.
Owala SmoothSip Slider Coffee Mug

As someone who often drinks coffee while commuting and walking my dog in the morning, I always love unwrapping a high-quality travel mug like this one from Owala. It’s made from stainless steel and has double-wall vacuum insulation to keep coffee hot for up to six hours and cold for up to 24. The mug has a leak-proof lid and a slide-top sip spout that prevents spills and splashes.

It’s available in 12-ounce, 20-ounce and 24-ounce sizes, and it comes in options with and without handles — I like the version without the handle to wrap my hands around when I’m cold and to easily place in a cup holder.
Simpletaste Milk Frother

Topping a standard cup of coffee with warm, foamy milk feels extra special, and you can help your giftee do exactly that at home with this gadget. It turns milk into warm dense foam, warm airy foam, cold foam or standard warm milk. Your loved one will select which option they want and let the milk frother work its magic — then, it automatically stops when it’s done. There are fill lines on the inside of the cup, which comes off of the base to rinse out in the sink. Your giftee can also use the milk frother to make hot chocolate and matcha lattes.
Yet Rambler 6-ounce Stackable Mugs

Sure, your loved one could brew their espresso shots into the cups their machine came with. But these mini Yeti mugs are an adorable upgrade, says Godio, who uses them while making lattes. Sold as a set of two, they’re made from stainless steel and double-wall vacuum insulated, so they keep espresso extra hot. They also have little handles for your loved one to grip while they sip or pour, and they’re dishwasher-safe and stackable for convenient cleaning and storage.
Oxo Brew Conical Burr Electric Coffee Grinder

Anyone who buys coffee grinds is missing out on the significantly better flavor of freshly ground beans. Make sure your giftee isn’t one of those people by getting them OXO’s grinder. Its removable hopper holds up to 12 ounces of beans and it’s UV-tinted to keep light out, thus preserving taste. Your loved one can choose from 15 grind settings and 43 micro-adjustments for the stainless steel blades, letting them pick the best option for espresso, Fresh press coffee and more.
Coffee-related gifts
Summer Fridays Iced Coffee Lip Butter Balm

Take your giftee’s love of coffee one step further by infusing the beverage into their lip balm. Summer Friday’s Lip Butter Balm, a top pick among the NBC Selected team, comes in an iced coffee flavor, which Cusack always reaches for. “I’ve tried almost every single flavor, and iced coffee is one of my top picks,” she says. “It has a subtle caramel scent that reminds me of my daily iced caramel latte, and the color is a sheer beige that looks great on all skin tones. The formula is hydrating and truly lasts for hours, but I find myself reapplying without even needing to because of how much I love the smell.”
Pop Chart The Compendious Chart of Coffee

Pop Chart’s coffee print teaches your loved one about how different beverages are brewed and what the exact ingredient ratios are. Plus, it’s beautifully hand-drawn, so they’ll be excited to show it off in their home. The print measures 20-by-16 inches — consider framing it for your giftee before giving it to them so they can hang it up as soon as they unwrap it.
See's Candies Chocolate Coffee Beans

I could eat an entire box of See’s Candies Chocolate Coffee Beans in one sitting — they’re that delicious. The little tin is stocking-sized, so I always toss one in for the coffee lovers in my life, or I pair it with other coffee-related products to make a themed basket.
Earl of East Gourmand Americano Cafe Candle

The rich Americano scent of this candle sold me when I tried it at Anthropologie, but the mug-shaped container made it even more worth it. It burns for about 60 hours, according to the brand, and it’s made with a soy blend and a cotton wick.
How to Taste Coffee: Develop Your Sensory Skills and Get the Most Out of Every Cup

I’m absolutely obsessed with coffee, but I don’t know anything about how to properly taste it, which may also be the case for your loved one. If so, this book should be their (and my) next read. It walks readers through what flavor notes are and how to identify them, as well as how people’s senses perceive coffee and what creates and affects its flavor. There are also 19 exercises in the book to help your giftee notice and talk about what they’re tasting while developing their palate.
Piecework Brew La-La Puzzle

Piecework’s Brew La-La Puzzle turns coffee into artwork and a relaxing analog activity your giftee can do with a group or by themselves. It has 1,000 pieces, and as they come together, your loved one will see more and more of the image: a Parisian cafe table filled with coffee mugs, spoons, splashes, latte art and more.
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has written gift guides for more than six years, including this one for coffee lovers, which I update annually with new picks. I’m a coffee lover myself who proudly admits to drinking at least three cups a day. I’m consistently testing coffee makers and accessories and I collect coffee-making gadgets and tools, as well as themed accessories. Beyond sharing my gift recommendations, I also gathered ones from other coffee-obsessed NBC Selected team members.

title: The ultimate gift guide for music lovers
summary: Shop the best gifts for music lovers, from headphones and record players to instruments and stocking stuffers, with picks from NBC Selected editors.
story: Music lovers can be surprisingly tricky to shop for. Whether they spend their weekends digging through crates at the record store, practicing guitar every night or simply can’t leave the house without headphones, music aficionados often already own the basics, and the gear they want next tends to be specific. A thoughtful gift can still hit the right note: an upgrade to their listening setup, something that helps them make music of their own or a fun accessory that celebrates their favorite artists.

To help you find something they’ll actually use, I gathered gift ideas for music fans of all ages, including options for adults and kids. I sourced items NBC Selected editors love, and I also pulled standout picks from popular brands we’ve covered before. Below, you’ll find headphones and speakers, turntables, instruments, stocking stuffers and more.

Best music gifts for adults
Apple AirPods 5

The AirPods 5 are a great gift for music lovers who listen on the go and pretty much anywhere else. They have up to 1.5 times more noise cancellation than the previous generation, adaptive audio that adjusts to your surroundings and up to 22 hours of total battery life with the USB-C wireless charging case. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans, who received a pair from the brand, also says they fit more comfortably than previous models: “I was pleasantly surprised that these pods with no rubber eartip didn’t budge.”
Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro

These earbuds are a great pick for Android users, especially those with a Galaxy phone. They support 24-bit hi-res audio and have a two-way speaker for richer sound, plus upgraded active noise cancellation to block out distractions. They’re also IP57-rated for dust and water resistance, and they come with interchangeable ear tips for a snug, comfortable fit.
Guitar Center Gift Card

Guitar Center offers lessons for a wide range of instruments, including guitar (electric and acoustic), bass, drums, keyboard, and even voice, so your recipient can pick whichever one excites them most. They also get to choose the day and time that fits their schedule and the instructor they like, making it easy to start playing. Just load the gift card with an amount you think makes sense to get them started — you can pick from one of the preset amounts up to $1,000 or put in a custom amount — then deliver it via email, text, Messenger or Whatsapp.
Soundcore Q30 by Anker Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones

The Soundcore Life Q30 headphones are a great budget-friendly gift for anyone who prefers over-ear headphones, with many of the features you’d find on pricier pairs. They have active noise cancellation, transparency mode, a folding design and a hard case for travel. But the real standout is the battery life, with up to 40 hours of playback with noise cancellation on and 60 hours with it off. And you get all of this for well under $100.
JBL Clip 5

Help a loved one bring their playlists everywhere with this portable speaker. The compact speaker has a built-in carabiner, so you can clip it to a backpack, belt loop or beach bag. It’s also IP67 dustproof and waterproof, gets up to 12 hours of battery life and can pair with other compatible JBL speakers for bigger sound. Evans says that this was her favorite portable speaker until her husband clipped it to his golf bag and she never saw it again. “And just like that, it became his favorite portable speaker,” she says.
Just the Ticket: Ticket Stub Organizer

This ticket stub organizer is a great pick for the sentimental people who never throw out a concert ticket. The binder holds up to 80 tickets in 20 acid-free plastic pages, each with lined inserts where they can jot down memories from the show, like the setlist or who they went with. A pocket inside the back cover stores programs and other keepsakes.
Victrola Journey Bluetooth Suitcase Record Player

This Victrola suitcase record player is a fun, beginner-friendly pick for anyone just starting a vinyl collection. The three-speed turntable plays 33, 45 and 78 RPM records through built-in stereo speakers, and you can also stream music from your phone via Bluetooth. It packs up into a retro-style suitcase with a carrying handle, and it has a headphone jack for private listening.
The Uncool: A Memoir

In “The Uncool,” Oscar-winning filmmaker Cameron Crowe looks back on his teenage years as a rock journalist, when he became Rolling Stone’s youngest-ever contributor at 15. The memoir chronicles the real-life events that inspired “Almost Famous,” including his time with Led Zeppelin, the Allman Brothers and David Bowie, and also covers films like “Fast Times at Ridgemont High” and “Jerry Maguire.”
Amazon Echo Dot

The Echo Dot is an affordable way to fill a bedroom, office or dining room with music. Just ask Alexa to play songs from streaming services like Amazon Music, Apple Music and Spotify, and the compact speaker delivers vibrant sound. It also works with Alexa+, Amazon’s upgraded AI assistant, and can control compatible smart home devices.
DuoMuo Anti-Skid Vinyl Drink Coasters

These DuoMuo coasters look like tiny vinyl records, with retro album-style designs that make for a fun conversation starter when guests come over. The set of six comes with a whimsical holder shaped like a record player, so they double as decor on a coffee table, shelf or bar cart, even when they’re not in use.
Stubhub Gift Card

A StubHub gift card is an easy way to treat someone to live music. Recipients can put it toward tickets to concerts, as well as sports games, theater and other live events, so they can pick a show they’re excited about. StubHub gift cards don’t expire, so there’s no pressure to use it before their favorite artist announces a tour.
Hitster: The Music Party QUIZ Game

Hitster is a music party game where players scan a card with the free Hitster app to play a song on Spotify, then guess when it was released and place it on their timeline. The first to correctly place 10 songs wins. The game includes more than 300 hits spanning the last 100 years and works for two to 10 players.
Tiny Vinyl Bob Marley & The Wailers

Tiny Vinyl makes mini 4-inch records that have one song on each side. This one featuring Bob Marley & The Wailers is a fun stocking stuffer for record collectors. It has “Three Little Birds” on one side and “Sun Is Shining” on the other, and it plays on most manual turntables. Tiny Vinyl is sold exclusively at Target and you can get a number of other artists, as well — including Ariana Grande, Noah Kahan, and Katseye.
Lola Portable CD Player

Lola’s portable CD player brings back the joy of listening to an album start to finish. The silver player has anti-skip protection so music won’t cut out on the go, up to 48 hours of battery life and a micro SD card slot for extra music. Evans, who tested this player, says another huge plus is that it doesn’t rely on WiFi or connectivity, so you can literally listen to it anywhere without worrying about buffering. It comes with polka dot earphones, though it works with any wired headphones.
Loop Experience 2 Ear Plugs

Loop Experience 2 earplugs are a thoughtful gift for concertgoers, musicians and festival fans. They reduce noise by 17 decibels while keeping music sounding clear, so the recipient can protect their hearing without missing out on the show. They come with four sizes of silicone ear tips for a comfortable fit, and a carrying case. They’re also nearly invisible from the front.
Best music gifts for kids
Loog Piano

This small piano is a great first instrument for young music lovers — I know because my 5-year-old daughter is obsessed with it. The 37-key digital piano has velocity-sensitive keys, built-in speakers and a rechargeable battery that lasts about eight hours. It also comes with flashcards and pairs with a learning app featuring video lessons and songs. I like that it’s compact and easy to tuck away when she’s done playing.
YLL Karaoke Machine

This mini karaoke machine is a fun gift for kids who love to sing. It comes with two wireless microphones, so they can duet with their favorite singing partner, and it connects to a phone or tablet via Bluetooth to play songs from any music app. It also has four voice-changing effects and is small enough to fit in a backpack.
Yoto Player (4th Generation)

The Yoto Player lets kids listen to music, stories and podcasts without a screen. They just pop in a Yoto Card or twist the new Green Button to play one of their favorites. The 4th-gen model has acoustically engineered stereo sound, a night light and an okay-to-wake clock, and you can make custom cards with your own playlists or recordings.
Lovevery The Music Set

Introduce toddlers to real music skills with this set, which includes six instruments, including pat bells, a pan flute and a concertina, plus a working metronome. Every instrument uses the pentatonic scale, so whatever kids play sounds harmonious. A color-coded rhythm and songs book teaches them to play simple tunes, and a play guide offers tips for each stage from 18 months to 4 years old.
Lego Editions Olivia Rodrigo's Vinyl

This 360-piece Lego set lets Olivia Rodrigo fans build a vinyl record decorated with nods to her career, including a megaphone, red lips, a butterfly and an autograph plaque. Spin the center to reveal extra stars and butterflies, then hang it on the wall or display it on a shelf. It also comes with an Olivia Rodrigo minifigure dressed in a look from her Sour tour.
Fisher-Price Rockin' Record Player Musical Toy

Fisher-Price’s Rockin’ Record Player lets preschoolers spin toy records just like a real turntable. It comes with five records featuring 20 songs across country, pop, hip-hop, mindfulness and kids’ classics, plus a display rack to store them. It’s a fun, retro way for little music fans ages 3 and up to choose what they want to listen to on their own.
VTech Kidi Star Drum Pad

This drum set allows kids ages 5 and older to choose from 20 drum styles, including rock, jazz and marching band, and play along with more than 30 built-in songs. Kids can also connect a phone via Bluetooth to drum along to their favorite music, record their performances and test their skills with three games and a coach mode.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I cover lifestyle and more. I have worked on gift guides for more than a decade. For this article, I compiled a list of the best music gifts of 2026, including highly-rated options, NBC Selected reader favorites and brands our editors love.
