title: ‘Looksmaxxing’ influencer Clavicular pleads not guilty to Massachusetts rape charges
summary: Braden Peters is accused of giving a teenage influencer alcohol and raping her while she was asleep in an incident on Cape Cod last year.
story: “Looksmaxxing” influencer Clavicular pleaded not guilty in Massachusetts court Thursday to criminal rape charges stemming from an alleged May 2025 incident at his family’s house on Cape Cod.

Clavicular, 20, whose real name is Braden Peters, was charged with rape, drugging someone for sexual intercourse and procuring liquor for someone under 21 years old, according to a criminal complaint filed on Sept. 8 in Orleans District Court in Barnstable County, Massachusetts.

Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, an 18-year-old influencer known online as Alorah or Alorah Ziva, alleged that last May, when she was 17 and in Massachusetts, Peters called her an Uber to his family’s home in Chatham, a beachfront town on Cape Cod.

When Mendoza was at Peters’ home, she alleged, he got her drunk with vodka during a livestream on Twitch and then raped her while she was asleep, the criminal complaint from the Chatham Police Department said. At the time, his mother and grandmother were allegedly in the house.
A representative and Peters’ lawyer declined to comment. Mendoza’s lawyer also declined to comment.

Peters’ lawyer filed a motion to dismiss the case following Thursday’s court appearance, arguing that Chatham police failed to present sufficient evidence to bring the charges. He has previously denied any wrongdoing and defended himself in a series of posts on X.

At his arraignment Thursday, a judge set bail at $10,000 after his defense team filed a memo in Orleans District Court on Wednesday asking for “fair and reasonable bail” in that amount. In it, his attorney argued that Peters is neither a danger to the community nor a flight risk and noted that he has no history of felony convictions.
For Subscribers
A court clerk confirmed Thursday that Peters paid the $10,000 bail in cash.

The criminal charges follow a civil suit Mendoza filed in Miami last year in which she accused Peters of sexual battery in connection with the alleged May 2025 incident on Cape Cod. In the civil suit, she also alleged he injected her face with a fat-dissolving substance not approved by the Food and Drug Administration during a November livestream in Florida.
A source familiar with the matter confirmed that the criminal charges stem from Mendoza’s allegations.
Earlier this month, Mendoza refiled her civil lawsuit and dropped the sexual assault allegations. At the time, her lawyer said it was to avoid interfering with the criminal case in Massachusetts.
For Subscribers

The Wednesday memo from Peters’ team also lays out his defense, arguing that Mendoza willingly created social media content with Peters and previously described him to her followers as “so nice.” The memo also says she continued to hang out with Peters and profit from their relationship after the alleged Cape Cod incident in May 2025.

The filing also includes a letter allegedly handwritten by Mendoza, in which she allegedly wrote, “Braden, you have my loyalty 100%. ... I admire the man you are,” and added that she wanted to continue working with Peters.
In screenshots of messages between Peters and Mendoza included in the filing, Mendoza appeared to imply she wanted to engage in a romantic relationship with Peters.
By early 2026, Peters’ lawyer alleged, Mendoza’s brand deals were drying up as Peters’ success continued to grow. She then filed the civil suit, the filing said.

When she reported the alleged rape to Chatham police in June 2026, she told officers she had not undergone a sexual assault forensic examination. She told police she told one friend about the alleged assault, then later changed her story and said she never told anyone about it, according to the memo.
This is not Peters’ first run-in with the law.

Peters and two other people were charged in Florida in April with shooting at an alligator. He and another person pleaded no contest to unlawfully discharging a firearm in public and were given six months of probation and ordered to serve 20 hours of community service, according to NBC South Florida.
He was also hospitalized in April in Miami after a suspected overdose, according to his representative.

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at rainn.org/get-help.

title: Teacher who survived Bend shooting tried to close door, ‘but the shooter was already there’
summary: Becky Drury was shot and seriously wounded by the gunman, who killed three children and another teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School in Oregon.
story: A teacher who was shot by a teenage gunman in a Bend, Oregon, elementary school last week said she saw the attacker and tried to shut the classroom door, “but the shooter was already there.”
Becky Drury said she was shot at close range in the rampage at Silver Rail Elementary School on Thursday.
“Lying on the floor, I saw that my left hand was almost completely severed from the gunshot, and my other arm was also severely injured,” Drury said in a statement Wednesday.
“I could not get up, defend myself, or protect anyone else,” she said. “So, I did the only thing I could do, which was to pretend to be dead in the hope he would not shoot me again.”
Three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a 25-year-old teacher were killed in the attack, which began around 1 p.m., officials said.

The gunman was fatally shot by a bystander who saw him fire at a truck and enter the school, police have said. The bystander followed the 16-year-old gunman and shot him as another teacher was wrestling with him over the weapon, according to police.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The motive remained under investigation Wednesday.

Investigators are looking into whether the shooter viewed any extremist material online, including material associated with “nihilistic violent extremism,” also known as NVE, two senior law enforcement officials briefed on the investigation told NBC News.
The gun was purchased legally, Bend police said Wednesday.
Police have said that it was a Maverick 88 pump-action 12-gauge shotgun and that the shooter used birdshot, buckshot and slugs.
Police have not said who purchased the gun. Two senior law enforcement officials previously told NBC News that the shooter’s mother bought it in August, around the time of his birthday.

“Bend Police detectives continue this complex investigation. They have served search warrants at the shooting suspect’s home, as well as on his electronic devices and his social media accounts on a variety of platforms,” police said in a statement Wednesday.
“That work continues, and it takes time,” the police department said.
Students in the greater Bend-La Pine Schools district returned to class Wednesday, although not at Silver Rail Elementary, where the shooting occurred.

“Through heartfelt artwork and messages of love, they are making sure every student who walks through the doors knows they are cared for, supported and loved,” the district said Tuesday as it prepared to welcome most students back.
Authorities have publicly identified two of the victims who were killed, 5-year-old Rhoam Summer and teacher Megan Lambert.
Drury, the wounded teacher, said in her statement that she heard a noise during last week’s shooting and went to investigate.
“Here is what I remember: Once I realized something was happening outside, I ran to see what was going on,” she said.
“I then saw the shooter and immediately ran back into the classroom. I turned to shut the door behind me, but the shooter was already there,” she said.
Drury said that there was nothing more she could have done and that “I was shot before I had any chance to act.”
“What happened in that classroom was unimaginable, and like so many in this community, my heart is broken for everyone affected by this tragedy,” she said.

“My thoughts are with those who were hurt, those we lost, their families, our school, and the Bend community,” she said. “I am truly grateful for the kindness and support we have received as we face the difficult days ahead together.”

title: John Anderson, twangy country singer known for ‘Seminole Wind,’ dies at 71
summary: In a music career spanning nearly 50 years, the “Swingin’” singer released more than 20 studio albums and earned three Grammy nominations.
story: John Anderson, the Grammy-nominated country crooner best known for the buoyant “Swingin’” and the plaintive “Seminole Wind,” died this week, according to posts on his official social media pages.
He was 71. No details of the cause of death were provided.
“It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend,” Anderson’s family wrote on his verified Facebook and Instagram accounts.

“To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special,” his family added in part.

In a music career spanning nearly 50 years, Anderson released more than 20 studio albums, landed dozens of singles on the Billboard country music charts and earned three Grammy Award nominations, including best country vocal performance in 1982.
In early 2024, Anderson was elected to the Country Music Hall of Fame. He said at a news conference that he was nearly at a loss for words over the “chance to be amongst this kind of greatness.”

“I’m trying to get a grasp on the reality of this happening to me,” Anderson said, Variety reported. “I want to thank all the fans who supported us through the last nearly 50 years. ... They ask just what this means and ... this is an institution that preserves greatness.”

John David Anderson was born in Apopka, Florida, on Dec. 13, 1954. He moved to Nashville, Tennessee, after having graduated from high school and picked up odd jobs while he was trying to break into the music business. He signed with Warner Bros. Records in the late ’70s after he caught attention for a string of local club appearances.

In the early 1980s, Anderson released two back-to-back self-titled studio albums featuring early hits like “Your Lying Blue Eyes” and “She Just Started Liking Cheatin’ Songs.” He hit the mainstream with his fourth studio album, “Wild & Blue” (1982), anchored by the high-wattage single “Swingin’.”

Anderson’s commercial fortunes went up and down across the ’80s, but he rebounded in the early ’90s thanks in part to the album “Seminole Wind.” The title track, a swampy and melancholy lament about environmental destruction, became one of his signature tunes.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“Ever since the days of old / Men would search for wealth untold / They’d dig for silver and for gold / And leave the empty holes,” he sang.

Anderson was a less visible presence in recent years, though he continued recording and released his final studio album, “Years,” in April 2020. The cover art featured a photo of Anderson gazing off into the distance in a black cowboy hat and white beard.
In a statement, Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum CEO Kyle Young praised Anderson as a “one-of-a-kind song stylist who proved that fresh innovations were best born from time-honored traditions.”
“Whether he borrowed inspiration from Lefty Frizzell’s vocal bends or the Florida swamp land, he brought dynamic distinction and creative soul to a world that needed to hear his voice,” Young said.
In social media posts, country music luminaries like Tim McGraw, Reba McEntire, Blake Shelton and Luke Combs mourned Anderson, too.

“I was talking with John Sunday night at the HOF ceremony,” McGraw wrote on Instagram, using the initials for the Hall of Fame. “He was in such good spirits. We talked, we laughed, we sang his songs that I loved so much together, just goofing off.”
“I am completely heartbroken by his passing,” McGraw added. “There will never be a stylist in music, any music, that was so defining as his. It’s just devastating.”

title: Mom whose son was found alive in morgue speaks out: ‘It’s an unexplainable feeling’
summary: Alexus Fiordilino said she thought her 18-month-old son, Vincent, was still breathing when she gave him a final hug, but the emergency room doctor insisted he was gone.
story: The mother of a toddler found alive in an Arizona hospital morgue in February more than five hours after he was pronounced dead said Wednesday she thought she heard him breathing when she hugged him goodbye.

But instead of listening to her gut, Alexus Fiordilino said, she believed the doctor who told her those were 18-month-old Vincent’s last gasps and that any further attempts to save him would just prolong his agony.
“As a mom you don’t want to hear that,” Fiordilino, 30, said in an interview. “I didn’t want him to suffer. It seemed to be they’d done everything they could. And then he called it.”
Fiordilino was referring to Dr. Aryan Toosi, who pronounced Vincent dead at 6:20 p.m. on Super Bowl Sunday at Mercy Gilbert Medical Center in Gilbert, Arizona.

A little over five hours later, Fiordilino said, police were questioning her and her husband, Angelo, when a detective burst into the room and told them that a medical examiner’s employee who had come to collect Vincent’s body had discovered he was still alive.
“My husband and I just screamed in relief,” she said. “We were praising the Lord. We were crying. To go from hearing he was gone and then finding out he isn’t gone, it’s an unexplainable feeling.”

Fiordilino spoke out more than eight months after her son’s remarkable story of survival after he nearly drowned in the family swimming pool made national headlines and sparked multiple investigations into what happened on Feb. 8.
The Gilbert Police Department had recommended filing child abuse charges against both parents for losing track of Vincent while a Super Bowl party was going on at their residence.
“Both admitted to smoking marijuana the morning of the drowning,” the police report said.
But Maricopa County Attorney Rachel Mitchell announced in July that the Fiordilinos would not be charged.

Fiordilino’s lawyer, John Brewer, said he plans to file a formal complaint this week against Toosi and the hospital. He said a review of Vincent’s medical records shows that critical test results that Toosi cited to justify ending efforts to save the child were not completed until after the toddler was declared dead.

“The parents were faced with having to decide whether to keep trying to revive their son, and the doctor provided them with false information,” Brewer said. “That’s beyond a conscious disregard for human life.”

Brewer’s office turned its records over to the Gilbert Police Department, which said it forwarded everything to the state attorney general’s office for review. The AG’s office said Wednesday that it has not made a decision to review this case.
Toosi’s lawyer, Scott Holden, released a statement in response.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“Dr. Toosi’s thoughts are with the young patient and family, and he wishes the child continued healing and recovery,” it said. “His commitment to delivering high-quality care has always been rooted in a desire to provide healing, safety and comfort to his community.”
Meanwhile, the hospital called the situation “heartbreaking” in a statement.

“Out of respect for the patient’s privacy, we cannot share any information and we are unable to comment on those involved in patient care,” it said. “Patient safety and exceptional care are our highest priorities.”
Asked how Vincent is doing now, Fiordilino said, “He’s getting better.”
Brewer said that while the boy is home with his family, he has many health challenges.
“Vincent is severely brain-injured,” he said. “He can’t swallow. He seizes up. He can’t sit up on his own or crawl.”

The tragic turn of events began around 5:38 p.m. Feb. 8 with a 911 call for help after Vincent was found floating face down in the family pool and a relative tried to revive him by performing CPR, according to a police report obtained by NBC affiliate KPNX of Phoenix.
Vincent was rushed to the emergency room at Mercy Gilbert Medical Center, where an ER team that included Toosi took over the effort to save him.
At 6:13 p.m., according to the report, Toosi went out to deliver bad news to the boy’s parents.
“As long as there are no objections, I’d like to call time of death,” Toosi said, according to the report.
Then, “at approximately 18:20 hours, Dr. Toosi called the time of death and requested a moment of silence.”
Just as Fiordilino told NBC News, police officers who had been in the ER said in the report that the child still appeared to be gasping for breath after he was declared dead.

A detective reported then hearing “another audible gasp” at around 7:18 p.m. as the ER workers were preparing to move Vincent from the trauma room to the “cold room” that serves as the hospital’s morgue and where the temperature is set at 36 to 39 degrees.
The same detective said that when he returned to photograph the body an hour later, he “again observed what appeared to be a gasp or air release.”
“The nurse again stated it was agonal breathing and explained it was due to compressions, oxygen, and possible pressure applied by family members while saying goodbye,” the report says.
And at 7:23 p.m., “the cold room door was closed,” the report says.
More than four hours later, when the medical examiner’s team arrived at 11:52 p.m. to retrieve the boy, “he was found breathing,” the report says.
“The family was notified immediately,” and the boy was airlifted to Phoenix Children’s Hospital.
Fiordilino said that when she saw her son again in the pediatric intensive care unit, “he was hooked up to all kinds of monitors and things.”
“He looked like a different baby,” she said. “It’s something I hope no other parent has to live through.”

title: Top adviser to Kennedy resigns from Trump administration
summary: Means, a key advocate for the “Make America Healthy Again” movement, had grown frustrated with a lack of progress on his policy goals, a source familiar with his departure said.
story: Calley Means, a top adviser to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and central advocate for the “Make America Healthy Again” movement, has resigned from the Trump administration.

“I am resigning from the White House with tremendous respect for President Trump and RFK — two historic figures who are committed to confronting a corrupt DC bureaucracy that is doing everything possible to protect the status quo,” Means said in a statement to NBC News. He posted a similar one on X.

Means was an adviser on Kennedy’s 2024 presidential campaign and a key architect of his MAHA agenda. He joined the White House early last year as a special government employee. He transitioned to a full-time role as senior adviser to the Health and Human Services Department after divesting from his wellness company, Truemed.
A person familiar with Means’ decision to resign said Means had been growing increasingly frustrated as he realized how little he could get done in Washington to advance his MAHA goals.

The final straw, the source said, was the lack of progress on rolling out a federal definition of ultraprocessed foods — one of Means’ biggest priorities. The administration teased a definition in August but has yet to release it.

The source also mentioned Trump’s executive order to boost the supply of the weed killer glyphosate in the U.S. (glyphosate is the key ingredient in Roundup), as well as some actions at the Environmental Protection Agency that have clashed with Kennedy’s agenda.
Trump’s EPA has, for example, weakened mercury emissions standards and rolled back drinking water limits for certain PFAS chemicals — actions the MAHA movement has largely opposed.
“We are grateful for Calley Means’ time in the Trump Administration. He has done a fantastic job for the MAHA movement,” White House spokesperson Allison Schuster said in a statement.

Frustrations over a lack of progress on MAHA goals have reverberated throughout the movement. Earlier this month, some supporters — including former members of Kennedy’s presidential campaign — accused the Trump administration of breaking nearly every promise made to them on food, agriculture and environmental health.

With less than two weeks left until the midterm elections, some dissatisfied MAHA supporters have threatened to abstain from voting. Some Democrats are seeking to make inroads with the movement in the final days of campaigning.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

One of the MAHA movement’s central beliefs is that corporations hold too much influence over the food supply and healthcare system. Many of its supporters, including Means, had hoped to see a greater crackdown on pesticides and artificial dyes, as well as more significant changes to vaccine policy that emphasize what some describe as “medical freedom” over universal recommendations.

On pesticides, a particular setback for the MAHA cause came in June, when the Supreme Court ruled that Bayer, the manufacturer of Roundup, didn’t need to warn consumers about a potential cancer risk associated with its product. The Trump administration had backed Bayer in the case.

President Donald Trump last year nominated Means’ sister, Casey Means, for surgeon general, but she faced scrutiny at her confirmation hearing over her lack of an active medical license and past comments questioning the safety of vaccines and birth control. Trump chose a new nominee, Dr. Nicole Saphier, in April.
Last month, at a talk Means gave at a MAHA summit in Washington, he said he was inspired by the way federal agencies had collaborated to advance the MAHA agenda, but he also acknowledged roadblocks.

“D.C. is a tough place. It’s a toxic place, and there’s a lot of complaints you can make about D.C.,” Means said. “But I am more optimistic today than I’ve ever been about what I feel is my life’s work of evangelizing the chronic disease crisis and empowering Americans who want to be healthy to address the root cause of disease.”

In his statement on Thursday, Means highlighted several policy wins for the MAHA movement during his tenure, including restricting soda purchases through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, fast-tracking research and review of psychedelics, urging food companies to voluntarily phase out certain dyes and overhauling the federal dietary guidelines to recommend less ultraprocessed food and more protein.
“More policy and cultural change has happened around these goals in the past 2 years than any time in history,” he wrote.

title: Miley Cyrus Helps Fan Shave Her Head Before Chemo Treatment: ‘Let’s Go Girl’
summary: Miley Cyrus recently stepped up to help a fan and fellow musician Cash Jacobs during an emotional battle with breast cancer.
story: Miley Cyrus recently stepped up to help a fan during an emotional battle with breast cancer.

The singer met with Cash Jacobs, a fellow musician, after one of her shows at the Hollywood Bowl earlier this month. During their hang, Cyrus helped Jacobs, who has Stage 3 breast cancer, shave her head in preparation for her chemotherapy treatments. The process was captured in a video that was shared on social media Oct. 21. And for Jacobs, the moment was profoundly meaningful.

“thank you @miley. For making me feel safe and comfortable, for giving me your time, and for being exactly who you are,” Jacobs wrote in the post’s caption. “It is a huge gift to continue to watch you grow and you are forever my biggest inspiration. Stay soft and strong 🤍”
In the video, Cyrus gives Jacobs some uplifting advice. The “Flowers” star also says a few words before the makeover.
“Thank you to the universe for bringing us together, and celebrating our connection and what music does for the world — it brings people like you and me together that may never meet,” Cyrus says.
The video then gets into the makeover process.
“Let’s go girl,” Cyrus says, before taking the buzzers to Jacobs’ head.
The pair share some light moments as well, with Cyrus remarking on how great Jacobs looks in the new ‘do.
“You got cute ears, you got a good-shaped head, you got a gorg face,” Cyrus says.

Jacobs initially got connected with Cyrus after she posted a video, sharing her breast cancer journey and calling on the singer to be the one to shave her head. The internet responded by tagging Cyrus and ultimately, the “Malibu” songstress came through.

In her Oct. 21 post, Jacobs explained that Cyrus not only flew her out to Los Angeles and gave her tickets to the show, but also helped her through “one of the scariest and most intimate moments of my life.”
“They say don’t meet your idols. Well I did. And it was everything and more,” Jacobs wrote.
She added that Cyrus’ music has always uplifted her during difficult moments in her life.

“And when they pass, I can listen to her songs and be reminded that I got through it and came out stronger,” Jacobs wrote. “Between major depressive episodes and finding out I have stage 3 breast cancer. I am lucky enough to have reached her and her team and been given this opportunity of a lifetime.”
Jacobs also thanked the internet for making it all happen, before praising Cyrus for her kindness.

“Miley is the softest, coolest, KINDEST, and most genuine human being I’ve ever had the privilege of meeting and spending time with. And not to mention her SHAVING MY F***ING HEAD!!!!! WHAT?!?” Jacobs wrote. “I want to hold on to this moment and to always remember the conversations we had and what they mean for me.”

Cyrus’ two nights at the Hollywood Bowl have been all-around emotional. The singer, whose recent performances marked her first solo shows since 2022, broke down as she paid tribute to her godmother, the late country legend Dolly Parton, on opening night.
“Me and Dolly, we are eternal,” Cyrus said, speaking to the crowd as she sat at the edge of the stage. “Nothing in this life could ever tear us apart.”

title: I’m a Forensic Psychologist Trained to Spot Liars. This Is What I’d Ask Elizabeth Holmes After Watching ‘You Can See Everything’
summary: This is what a forensic psychologist trained to spot liars thinks of Elizabeth Holmes in “You Can See Everything.”
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this edition, a forensic psychologist weighs in on “You Can See Everything.”
Spoilers ahead for “You Can See Everything.”

“You Can See Everything” has audiences twisting to identify truths and lies. Filmmakers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim moved into Elizabeth Holmes’ house 34 days before she was set to surrender to federal prison for an 11-year sentence related to defrauding investors in relation to her biotech company, Theranos.
John De La Torre, a forensic psychologist who specializes in criminal work, scams and con artists, is uniquely well-suited to weigh in on who was telling the truth among all the players.
But he couldn’t.

“When I left that movie, I left feeling that all I saw was a game,” De La Torre tells TODAY.com. “All I saw was Nathan Fielder’s game to try to show me what he considers to be the truth, but isn’t necessarily the full truth. I see Billy and I see Elizabeth Holmes. I see the games that they play.”
De La Torre is trained to see deception and malingering. But he says this isn’t humans’ strong suit. “We’re not very good at detecting who is lying to us,” he says.
That’s what makes parsing this documentary as an audience member difficult. “Everything that is going on is masked by the color of the possibility that we are being lied to,” he says.
The Questions a Forensic Psychologist Would Have Asked Elizabeth Holmes

If De La Torre were in Fielder’s shoes, he says he would start with talking to Holmes about her defining relationships: “What she understands about them. Are the relationships that she has transactional, and what does that transaction look like for her? How does she know that someone likes her or doesn’t like her?”
While listening, he looks for consistency in people’s stories. “Consistent people tell the truth. Inconsistent people lie,” he says.

He paid attention to Fielder’s lines of questioning. While he’s “pretty good at exploring and following up,” he noticed some of the things he didn’t follow up on, like Holmes’ father’s disclosure of her previous sexual assault.

He also would take an approach similar to his work as a forensic psychologist, De La Torre assesses people accused of a crime using sanity and competency evaluations, to see if there is a mental disorder that a person may have.
Here’s Where He Comes Down on Elizabeth Holmes
After seeing the movie, De La Torre made up his mind about Holmes.
“I think she legitimately thinks she did nothing wrong,” he says. “I’m not even sure she knows.”

“I think she operates under the assumption that she needs to win or that something positive needs to happen. So long as she’s on the positive side, she’s willing to engage in whatever behavior she needs to engage in. That includes potentially making someone else be the bad guy,” she says.
Holmes swears to Fielder that she’s never knowingly told a lie, despite being convicted of fraud in 2022.

For a bit of background, Holmes dropped out of Stanford and became the youngest female billionaire thanks to Theranos, the biotech company she founded, based on a technology that could purportedly run tests on a single drop of blood.

Holmes was convicted on four federal charges of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors what the Edison blood-testing machine could actually do. In her trial, she denied her product was defective.
Even if she swears she’s not lying, De La Torre considers Holmes a con artist.

“I think she truly believed in the work that she was doing, but therein lies the con because it doesn’t actually do the things that she claimed that it did,” De La Torre says. “She made other people believe that it could already do those things. And it is through that belief, that confidence that she had, that that was the con game that she was playing.”
Ultimately, De La Torre describes Holmes’ con as: “Making someone else believe that they are what she needs in order to be successful.”
What the Shower Scene Says About Billy Evans

Billy Evans, Holmes’ partner with whom she shares two children, has ample screen time in the movie, often intervening and sharing his own opinions. At one point, the camera catches Evans fully nude in the shower. It’s a telling moment, according to De La Torre.
“His willingness to expose himself to another man suggests that what he craves is attention,” he says.
He often gets attention by “saying something outlandish, saying something ridiculous, saying something that clearly demonstrates that he doesn’t care about other people.”
Whereas Holmes often “appears as though she’s executing human programming,” Evans knows how to feel and emote more easily.
The ‘Only Person’ With an Objective View
According to De La Torre, the only person with an objective and unbiased view of the action is Amanda Seyfried.

“It’s important to understand that no one in this film is telling the truth, except for Amanda Seyfried, and the only truth she tells is by calling out all of the other games that are being played whenever anybody is talking,” De La Torre says.

Seyfried played Holmes in the Hulu series “The Dropout,” and reprises the role in the documentary, all while helping Fielder investigate what’s really going on between Holmes and Evans. Her onscreen presence is captivating and animated, acting as a stand-in for the audience.
“I think she’s the one that calls out everything, all of the nonsense whether it’s from Billy or whether it’s from Nathan. I think Amanda Seyfried is the person to really listen to,” he continues.
An Exercise in Confirmation Bias
“You Can See Everything”? More like, “You Can See Some Things, Kind Of.”
De La Torre says that if you walk out of the theater confused, it’s only because you recognize Holmes, Evans and Fielder all had an agenda.
“Every single one of them is playing the game. And leaving confused just tells me that you are now also aware that what you are seeing may not be fully everything, “he says.

title: Daisy Edgar-Jones’ Dad, Who Created ‘Big Brother,’ Gave Her This Talk Before She Got Famous
summary: Daisy Edgar-Jones’ father, a TV executive who co-created Big Brother, gave her this talk before she got famous.
story: British television executive Philip Edgar-Jones witnessed plenty of people rocket to fame while at the helm of the long-running reality show “Big Brother,” so he had some words of wisdom for his daughter when she was on the verge of stardom herself.

Actor Daisy Edgar-Jones, 28, spoke with Jenna Bush Hager on the Oct. 22 episode of her “Open Book with Jenna” podcast about the advice her father gave her before the Emmy-winning series “Normal People” was released in 2020.
She noted how on “Big Brother,” “individuals would come in anonymous and leave very, very famous,” so her father had experience seeing people make that transition during his 10 years with the show.
When “Normal People” was released during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, he reached out to her over the phone and on video calls to prepare her for what might lay ahead.

“(He) essentially said, there might be some things that will shift for you, and here’s just some words I’ve learned of wisdom. Which is that you might not change, but the world around you might, and the way people interact with you might, and so remembering that you haven’t changed, that you are who you are and you are the same person that you were pre all of this is really important to keep your feet on the floor.”
“Normal People,” based on a bestselling novel by Sally Rooney, was Edgar-Jones’ breakout role, so the advice was timely.

She said her father advised her to “know that you’re an individual amongst lots of people with all their own stuff going on and inner lives, and it’s really important to remember to keep your feet planted very firmly on the floor.”
The “Sense and Sensibility” star remains “grateful” for those words of wisdom. She also hopes to take a cue from her father in another way.

“Every time I meet anyone who’s worked with my dad, they always say he’s the nicest man in television, which is such a lovely legacy,” she said. “And I’m really proud of him for that. I’m proud of him for so many things, but I suppose if I’ve learned from that, it would be nice if that could be my legacy in some way that when you interact with someone, you leave a nice taste in their mouth or a nice flavor. That would be something I’m very proud of.”

title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Stars Stew and Jax Reveal Where They Stand After Awkward Breakup
summary: “Love Is Blind” Season 11 stars Jax and Stew tell TODAY.com how their relationship has unfolded since the show ended.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “Love Is Blind” Season 11 below…
After her ghosting moment that went viral, Jacqueline “Jax” Guelli decided to reunite with ex-fiancé Scott “Stew” Stewart in the newest episodes of “Love Is Blind” to explain her hasty departure.
So far, the most talked about moment of Season 11 of the Netflix reality dating show has been Jax’s reaction after meeting Stew for the first time.

Following their engagement in the pods, Jax and Stew saw each other face-to-face, and the feelings were no longer mutual. She informed the producers that she wanted to leave the show immediately and return home, without breaking up with Stew in person. Producers told him about her abrupt exit, and shared the news that Jax didn’t want to leave any contact information for Stew.

But in Episode 6, the two had a sit-down in Boston to unpack their broken engagement. Stew asked why Jax didn’t want to have a conversation before leaving. She said she should have spoken to him and he didn’t deserve how she treated him. She also shared that her family and friends encouraged her to chat with him.
Jax then told Stew she expected to be “blown away” by their connection in real life, but she wasn’t.
In response, Stew asked, “Is that our cue to leave?” They had another confusing exit and didn’t appear again in the second batch of episodes.
Stew reveals the status of their relationship in an interview with TODAY.com.

“I think the pods was such an intense experience, and it accelerates relationships so much that I think we both kind of lost our bearing once we got back to the real world,” he says. “I think it just took some time for each of us to resettle, reconnect with our friends and family (and) reconnect with normal life.”
As for where the two currently stand, he says, “Since then we’ve been great friends, and the relationship has continued.”
In a separate interview, Jax clarifies to TODAY.com that it wasn’t the opinions of her friends and family that pushed her to meet Stew on camera.
“We definitely needed to talk. And I was happy and I was excited to see him,” she says.
The two will likely reveal more about how they mended their relationship at the upcoming Season 11 reunion. The date of the reunion has yet to be announced.

title: Craig Melvin Wins His People’s Sexiest Man Alive Poll ... and Gets Crowned on TODAY!
summary: Craig Melvin has won the “hotter than your cup of coffee in the morning” category in the People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll.
story: Craig Melvin is hot!
The TODAY co-anchor has won the “hotter than your cup of coffee in the morning” category in the People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll.
Craig beat out Michael Strahan, Gio Benitez and Vladimir Duthiers for the title, with readers voting on the question: “Which of these morning hosts is hotter than your first cup of coffee?”

“We we are happy to announce, ladies and gentlemen, that our friend Craig here is officially hotter than a cup of coffee this morning,” Carson Daly announced on the Oct. 22 episode of TODAY. “You have been voted People magazine’s sexiest morning show host.”
Craig was recognized for his feat with a towel with the “sexiest man alive” logo on it, along with a crown and a sash.
“Come on, you’re the king,” Al Roker said.
“Long may you reign,” Savannah Guthrie said.
Carson made a joke that Craig got the towel because the magazine knows he sweats a lot.
“Now we know why he sweats. It’s because he’s so hot,” Savannah said.
Craig, who was playfully egged on to give a speech, took the award in stride.
“Glad it’s over,” he said.
“Thanks to my mom and my wife who voted at least 100, 200 times, for sure,” he added.
His wife, Lindsay Czarniak, was also thrilled with the honor.
“He’s just sexy in everything she does,” she said when she appeared from home on the 3rd hour of TODAY on Oct. 22.
“This doesn’t mean that you have to stop doing things, but it’s sort of like you know everything can get a little sexier, like sexy cooking, right?” she joked.
After some jokes about Craig doing chores around the house while shirtless, Lindsay then turned a little bit more serious.

“One of the things I thought of first was my grandma, she’s going to be so excited because she lives for watching you and this show,” she said. “And I tried to call her this morning because I was like, ‘You’re just not going to believe it.’ And this is really cool.”
She ended with a message for her husband. “I do think you’re sexy, but I am really proud of you because you know you’re sexy at heart, as well,” she said.
Craig was nominated for the honor last month and took it in stride. His co-anchors became some of his biggest cheerleaders, with Savannah Guthrie encouraging viewers to “vote early and often.”
“Am I being punk’d right now?” Craig said on TODAY Sept. 30 of his nomination.
Lindsay also made sure to campaign for him. Craig and Lindsay, who have been married since 2011, share two children, Delano, 12, and Sybil, 9.

“He is an amazing dad, tremendous husband, teammate, partner, always so supportive and encouraging,” she said in an Instagram reel posted Oct. 12. “He makes a mean chili ... he is a pro at candle-making. He is really good at debating. This is true — and I mean in the most positive of ways.
“But beyond that, he is someone who really cares about where he’s from, leaves people feeling really good about themselves in his presence,” she continued.

“And beyond all those things that make him sexy on the outside — like, let’s be honest, the dimple, guys, it’s the dimple — I think it’s his character and his makeup on the inside that make us think that really, you know, he’s the sexiest man alive.”
Craig had previously appeared in People’s Readers’ Choice poll. In 2023, he was nominated for sexiest morning show host, but lost out to Mark Consuelos.

title: How to Read All 18 of Sarah J. Maas’ Books In Order
summary: So you’re considering jumping down the rabbit hole that is author Sarah J. Maas’ sprawling catalog of romantasy books.
story: So you’re considering jumping down the rabbit hole that is author Sarah J. Maas’ sprawling catalog of romantasy books. You’ve heard about her, perhaps through BookTok or your reading buddies or her legions of fans who can’t get enough. You know about her three series — “Throne of Glass,” “A Court of Thorns and Roses” and “Crescent City”— and her forthcoming books, “A Court of Splintered Harmony” and “A Court of Forgotten Melody,” have only heightened your interest.
So you want to join in on the fun. But where do you begin? And what order should you be reading?
If you’re overwhelmed — 18 books might do that — fret not. We’ll help you get started.
More on Sarah J. Maas and ‘ACOTAR’
Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All Rise‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ Books 6 and 7 Titles and Covers Revealed by Sarah J. Maas
Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All Rise
‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ Books 6 and 7 Titles and Covers Revealed by Sarah J. Maas
Sarah J. Maas Books to Read First
There are two key things to note when getting started:
It doesn’t matter if you read the “Throne of Glass” books or the “ACOTAR” books first.
Read the “ACOTAR” books before you pick up the “Crescent City” books.

If you’re debating whether to start with “Throne of Glass” or “ACOTAR,” it depends on your preference: “ACOTAR” is romance forward — if you lean toward that genre, start there. “Throne of Glass” is big on the epic fantasy elements — you lean toward that, start there.
‘Throne of Glass’ Series Reading Order

“Throne of Glass” is Maas’ first book she published in 2012, and it eventually became a series of eight books in total. Maas on her website lists her preferred reading order, which is the publication order. It looks as such:
“Throne of Glass” (2012)
“Crown of Midnight” (2013)
“The Assassin’s Blade” (2014)
“Heir of Fire” (2014)
“Queen of Shadows” (2015)
“Empire of Storms” (2016)
“Tower of Dawn” (2017)
“Kingdom of Ash” (2018)

“The Assassin’s Blade” is a prequel (technically a collection of novellas) that Maas published after the first two books were released and features characters that crop up later the book series. Because of that, some argue that reading the series in the story’s chronological order is beneficial. If you choose to do that, Maas and her publishers at Bloomsbury have said that’s fine too — it doesn’t spoil anything.

There’s a community of fans who created a way for people to read “Empire of Storms” and “Tower of Dawn” at the same time, by switching back and forth between chunks of chapters. These two penultimate books take place in two different locations but at the same point in the story. For those interested in the tandem read, here is a PDF that you can refer to.
‘ACOTAR’ Series Reading Order

“A Court of Thorns and Roses,” also known by its acronym “ACOTAR,” is typically the gateway into the SJM universe. The highly anticipated sixth and seven books in the series were announced in August and will be released Oct. 28, 2026, and Jan. 12, 2027, respectively.
The “ACOTAR” series should be read in publishing order, which is also the story’s chronological order:
“A Court of Thorns and Roses” (2015)
“A Court of Mist and Fury” (2016)
“A Court of Wings and Ruin” (2017)
“A Court of Frost and Starlight” (2018)
“A Court of Silver Flames” (2021)
“A Court of Splintered Harmony” (Oct. 28, 2026)
“A Court of Forgotten Melody” (Jan. 12, 2027)
‘Crescent City’ Series Reading Order

The “Crescent City” series contains three novels (though Maas told TODAY in 2023 that a fourth is on the horizon). As Maas and her publishers at Bloomsbury have noted, “you may find the ‘Crescent City’ reading experience more rewarding if you pick up the ‘Court of Thorns and Roses’ series first.”
Like “ACOTAR,” the recommended reading order for “Crescent City” is the publishing order:
“House of Earth and Blood” (2020)
“House of Sky and Breath” (2022)
“House of Flame and Shadow” (2024)

title: Our 1 Big Question for Jackie Tohn During Commercial: Are Sasha and Esther End Game in ‘Nobody Wants This’?
summary: Jackie Tohn talks about whether Sasha and Esther will end up together in Season 3 of “Nobody Wants This” and what she makes of Morgan and Sasha.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.
Warning: This story contains spoilers for Season 3 of “Nobody Wants This.”
Esther breaks free from her marriage in the third season of “Nobody Wants This.” But does she like what’s on the other side?
Jackie Tohn, in an interview with TODAY.com, says she’s just like viewers in that she comes to new seasons excited to find out what happens to her character.

“People always ask me, ‘What do you want to happen?’ And I’m like, ‘I’m like you guys. I’m like the fans. I want to see what the showrunners and writers come up with. It’s not for me to say what happens.’ It’s really exciting,” she says.
In the third season, Esther moves forward with her separation from Sasha (Timothy Simons). Living alone for the first time, she gets a real estate degree and finds connections via online dating.

Meanwhile, Sasha explores that long-simmering tension between him and Morgan (Justine Lupe), the sister of his brother’s fiancée. After that, Sasha and Esther have one night together that makes it all the more complicated.

It comes to a head in the finale, when Esther learns about Morgan and Sasha (and so does Sasha’s mom), making Joanne (Kristen Bell) and Noah (Adam Brody) seem like the most stable couple in the group.
Below, we unpack that love triangle and the plot twists that ensue.

In Season 2, Esther sort of threatened to be a good time. She wasn’t yet, but she was like, “I’m fun too. Why is everyone else fun? I’m fun.” And in Season 3, she’s really putting her money where her mouth is and being like, “What does my life look like outside of being a wife and a mother?”

She gets a job for the first time since she’s had a kid. She gets her real estate license. She goes on the apps. She tries to figure out, if she had asked herself all of these big life questions, (where) would she be? Would this be where she’d be? What would she want to do? Who would she want to be with? And maybe it is Sasha. It’s a huge, huge season of self-discovery, growth for her.
It’s a huge growth season for him. I think for Noah and Joanne, it’s very “champagney” and delicious.

Meanwhile, Sasha’s sort of forced to face the music. Then he makes the first mature decision of his life, where he’s in this situation with Morgan and he’s like, “I don’t know what this is, or if this is anything, but certainly right now is not the time.” And so he’s making all these mature decisions, which I think before he maybe didn’t have the balls to do.
Completely different. From Morgan he gets (something) fun, wild.

With Esther, there’s obviously love there. There’s history. There’s stability. They have a daughter, and I do think Sasha and Esther love each other. Because he was a little bit gentler, he needed a fire lit under his ass, and that fire was Esther. I think a lot of people need that kind of partner that’s going to push them to be better, and Esther does all of that for him.
Morgan has always been this fun friend, but now maybe there is something more there. There is a depth there where they both are the sort of the “loser” sibling, but they see something in each other.
I think I have skin in the game. But in my brain, I think it’s Esther. I really do. I must think that because I’m her. I just feel like in my heart, Sasha and Esther go together.

Bina for sure. Esther can be as upset as she wants, but she made her bed, right? She literally said to him, “I am going to go do this. You should too.” So he did. And yeah, she’s hurt. But Bina’s like, “Great, now this son is ruining the family.”

I think that it’s sort of happening in that she’s always been so serious, and I’m so goofy. I like that in Season 3, she’s a little bit more like, “Oh my God, I’m nervous. What do I do? Where do I go?” She doesn’t have it as together as she does in Season 1 and Season 2. She’s just the boss and she knows where everything is. She knows how to be and what to do. And in Season 3, she’s a little bit more fumbling. I think it’s sweet to show her vulnerability in that way.

title: Who Is Koschei the Deathless? What to Remember About the Next ‘ACOTAR’ Villain
summary: When author Sarah J. Maas announced the next two installments of her “A Court of Thorns and Roses” series this summer, both books’ synopses named only one specific character: Koschei the Deathless.
story: When author Sarah J. Maas announced the next two installments of her “A Court of Thorns and Roses” series this summer, both books’ synopses named only one specific character: Koschei the Deathless.

If you’re among those who reacted with an echoing “who?”, that’s understandable. The last book in the series, “A Court of Silver Flames,” had us focused on Blood Rites and Valkyries and all that Nesta-Cassian romancing. The looming threat facing the world? Consider it reader amnesia.

The gist: While the prior books had Feyre, Rhysand and the Night Court gang battling and defeating Hybern, an island west of Prythian whose king wanted to reclaim the Fae’s dominance, the team is now pivoting to a new big bad who’s way more dangerous.
For those in need of a quick Koschei refresher, we’ve got you. Here’s a summary before heading into “ACOTAR” Book 6, “A Court of Splintered Harmony.”
Read More on “ACOTAR”

Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All RiseHow to Read ‘ACOTAR’ Author Sarah J. Maas’ Books in OrderInside ‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ and the Sprawling Romantasy Universe That Has TikTok Obsessed
Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All Rise
How to Read ‘ACOTAR’ Author Sarah J. Maas’ Books in Order
Inside ‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ and the Sprawling Romantasy Universe That Has TikTok Obsessed
Koschei is a ‘Death-God’ and Sibling to the Bone Carver and Weaver
Let’s start by going back a few books to the third in the series, “A Court of Wings and Ruin,” in which Koschei receives his first mention.

In Chapters 22 and 23, Cassian and Feyre are visiting the Prison, a place beneath a mountain where dangerous beings are locked away, to recruit an insidious creature called the Bone Carver to fight alongside Prythian in the war against Hybern. They are prepared to offer the Carver a way back to the world from which he originated, but the Carver insists his home is long gone and wishes to stay within the safety of his prison cell.

He’s hiding, he says, from his two powerful siblings: his twin sister, Stryga, also known as the Weaver of the Wood, and their older brother, Koschei. Both “fell” into this world with him long before Prythian existed. Together they are “death-gods,” meaning they feed on life itself, but he says his brother and sister are more powerful than he.
Koschei is Confined to a Far Away Lake
During that conversation at the Prison, the Carver tells Feyre and Cassian that Stryga and Koschei were worshipped and feared by the ancient Fae before they were captured by a “clever” Fae warrior.
“She could not kill them in the end — they were too strong. They could only be contained,” the Carver says. “I knew that long before she ever trapped them — took it upon myself to find my way here.”
His siblings have been imprisoned since: Stryga is confined to a cottage in Prythian’s unmapped area called the Middle. Koschei is bound to a lake on the continent east of Prythian.
Hybern, with the Cauldron’s possession, ends up taking out the Bone Carver and Stryga in the war. Koschei, meanwhile, is still at his lake, but he’s been cooking up a plan of his own.
Koschei Enslaves One of the Human Queens

In Chapter 33 of “A Court of Wings and Ruin,” Elain, who’s a seer, shares a vision about a “sorcerer-lord” who holds captive one of the human queens who allied with Hybern in the war. She lives as a firebird by day, human by night, and the sorcerer-lord also possesses an “onyx box” that’s more vital to him than anything.
“He keeps other girls — others so like her,” Elain says. “... He keeps them all at the lake.”

In Chapter 54, readers learn more about what happened to this human queen. Her name is Vassa, and, when she refused to join the queens in allying with Hybern, they found a death-lord who enslaves and curses young women and gave her over to him. All this time, the human queens have been claiming she’d fallen ill.

Vassa then shows up in Chapter 72 to fight Hybern in the war and later explains that she was able to come because the Archeron sisters’ father cut a deal with her keeper to release her from the lake temporarily. What exactly that deal is, she does not say.
It’s not until the next book, “A Court of Silver Flames,” that Vassa reveals her keeper is Koschei.
Koschei Wants to Be Free — to Do What?

In “A Court of Silver Flames,” the war against Hybern is won but the Night Court is hearing about bigger threats. In Chapter 7, Vassa, who’s been residing in Prythian’s mortal lands during her time away from the lake, tells her allies that Koschei would do anything to be liberated and may be leveraging a relationship with one of the other human queens, Briallyn.

“I fear what may happen if he ever gets free of the lake,” she tells Cassian. “If he sees this world on the cusp of disaster and knows he could strike, and strike hard, and make himself its master. As he once tried to do, long ago.”

In Chapter 20, Azriel learns more about what they’re up to: Briallyn, who, back in the second book, gleefully jumped into the Cauldron to become immortal but came out a crone, is trying to find her way back to the Cauldron to “retrieve her youth.” Koschei is helping her cause — by pointing her in the direction of the Dread Trove, the magical items connected to the Cauldron — so he too can use the Cauldron to unbind him from the lake.
Briallyn is defeated by Nesta at the end of “A Court of Silver Flames” — but Koschei’s scheming is just beginning.

title: I’m a Therapist Trained to Read Facial Cues. This Is Why ‘You Can See Everything’ Is So Unsettling
summary: A psychologist reacts to You Can See Everything, why it’s such an unsettling experience and the body language of Elizabeth Holmes, Nathan Fielder and Billy Evans.
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this edition, a licensed therapist with a degree in cognitive neuroscience weighs in on “You Can See Everything.”
Spoilers ahead for “You Can See Everything.”
If you walk into the “You Can See Everything” expecting answers, you might come out of the theater with more questions.

And if you walk into “You Can See Everything” as a clinical psychologist who studies body language and facial cues, you immediately get another ticket. At least that was the case for Morgan Starr-Riestis, who, as of Oct. 20, saw the documentary following Elizabeth Holmes twice since its Oct. 16 release.
Starr-Riestis, a therapist who has a specific training in nervous system regulation, body language and facial cues, says the movie is an “unsettling” experience.

“We’ve learned to track each other’s facial expressions and micro expressions. To be honest, as somebody that’s trained in this, it was hard to read, especially the first half of it,” she tells TODAY.com.

The documentary, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, opens 34 days before Holmes, convicted in 2022 on four counts of fraud related to her work with her health technology start-up Theranos, surrenders to prison.

Already attracting Oscar buzz (unexpected, considering a documentary has never been up for best picture), critics are calling it “a fascinatingly intimate portrait of a deluded or disingenuous scammer.”

Famous for becoming the world’s youngest female billionaire, Holmes was convicted by a jury in California of four federal charges of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors what Theranos’ blood-testing Edison machines were actually capable of doing.

Fielder attempts to investigate whether Holmes knowingly defrauded investors — whether she intentionally lied. Holmes dodges the characterization in the doc, attesting she has never told a lie before, not even a white lie. Another telling moment involving a famous comedy sketch might indicate she doesn’t pick up on social cues.

But viewers are divided as to whether Holmes is as naive as she seems. And insiders are not convinced by Holmes’ feigning innocence. John Carreyrou, the former Wall Street Journal reporter who shattered Theranos’ image of a revolutionary blood-testing device through his reporting, is skeptical, as is whistleblower Tyler Shultz. Carreyrou called it a “great film” but said there’s “no chance” Holmes was just “along for the ride” with Theranos. Shultz wrote in a review for Stat News, a health and science publication, that she’s “still lying.”

For psychologists, it’s no surprise the film leaves audiences twisted as to who to trust. Is it Fielder, who turns himself into a character? Is Holmes somehow under the sway of her fiancé, Billy Evans, with whom she shares two kids?

Starr-Riestis caveats that body language isn’t always an accurate read of how someone is feeling. “Some people who have trauma histories or grew up around an angry caregiver, for example, can actually be hyper-sensitive to micro expressions more than someone who didn’t because they learned from a young (age) a certain furrow of a brow might be dangerous,” she says.
Not everyone is good at picking up social cues, too. “There’s also a wide range of reasons why someone might not read facial expressions as well — autism as an example,” she says.
Still, with those caveats in mind, here’s what she found on both watches of “You Can See Everything,” all six hours of it.
The ‘Dissociative Gaze’
Starr-Riestis called Holmes’ wide, unblinking stare during conversations with Fielder an example of the “dissociative gaze.”

“When our eyelids are pulled back like that and we’re unblinking, that’s usually a sign of fear or overwhelm. When you pair it with a smile, the mismatch is naturally unsettling. Our nervous systems just register it as something off,” she says.
A ‘Socially Disorienting’ Conversation Style That ‘Leaves Us on Alert’
The conversation style between Fielder and Holmes is unusual enough for it to be notable. Fielder’s style is “socially disorienting,” she says.

“He lets pauses hang, keeps his delivery flat, and doesn’t smooth over awkward moments the way most instinctively do. Normally, those small social cues tell us how to feel, so without them we’re left to read every interaction raw,” she says.
On Holmes’ end, her “words, tone and expression often don’t seem to match: warm, caring content delivered with a steady, still, intense gaze.”
“When someone’s verbal and nonverbal signals don’t line up, our nervous system registers the mismatch before we can name it, and we go on alert,” she says.
Amanda Seyfried’s ‘Warmth’ Is a Contrast

For Starr-Riestis, the movie changed in the third act when Amanda Seyfried unexpectedly enters the scene. Seyfried portrayed Holmes in the Hulu scripted series “The Dropout.” She reprises the role in “You Can See Everything” and also interacts with Evans, Fielder and Holmes (via a prison phone call) directly.
“What was a refreshing change was having Amanda’s facial cues. She’s so easy to read. You can watch the way her eyebrows rustle when she’s disturbed,” Starr-Riestis says.
Seyfried’s “warmth” is “absent in both Nathan and Elizabeth,” Starr-Riestis says. “To have both him and Elizabeth in the same room, you’re void of a lot of the normal social cues.”
Billy Evans ‘Staring Off’ and ‘Leaving the Room’
Starr-Riestis paid attention to Evans’ movements in the movie.
Evans, who met Holmes before she was indicted, frequently clashed with Fielder in the name of trying to protect Holmes. But some — including Seyfried — say he was controlling.
“You could see him staring off a lot. It felt like he was really trying to keep his anger in,” she says.
She says it seemed like he was trying to “be on his best behavior,” but he “had a hard time hiding it.”
“He would need to leave at certain points or remove himself because it felt like he was just keeping it all bottled (in),” she says.
‘Not Enough Cues’ to Find Out What’s Real
The movie leaves viewers feeling like they don’t know who, or what, to trust.
“I don’t have enough cues to figure out what’s real in this situation,” Starr-Riestis says.
The movie points to an “uncomfortable truth” she says we need to live with: “Each of us are living in our subjective universes.”

“I see it as a Venn diagram. There is overlap in our experience to where we can agree on things and have some sort of shared truth,” she says. “But you can’t see into someone else’s brain and perspective and perception. We can only know a portion of the truth.”

title: ‘10 Things I Hate About You’ Star David Krumholtz Shares Why He Missed the ‘DWTS’ Reunion
summary: David Krumholtz is explaining why he wasn’t able to join his fellow “10 Things I Hate About You” co-stars during their reunion on “Dancing With the Stars.”
story: David Krumholtz is explaining why he wasn’t able to join his fellow “10 Things I Hate About You” co-stars during their reunion on “Dancing With the Stars.”

The actor, who portrayed Michael in the ‘90s rom-com, was missing from the ballroom during the Oct. 20 Dedication Night episode when Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Gabrielle Union, Larisa Oleynik, Andrew Keegan and Susan May Pratt supported Julia Stiles’ emotional tribute to the late Heath Ledger.
Krumholtz shared in an Instagram video Oct. 21 that he would’ve loved to reunite with the cast, but he is currently across the country working on his next project.

“Good morning, here I am in the Catskill Mountains, upstate New York. Fall foliage in full effect,” he said as he panned the camera to show his surroundings. “I am here shooting a film. I could not be in LA for ‘Dancing With the Stars’ last night. I would have loved, loved, loved to have been there.”
He praised the “10 Things I Hate About You” cast before applauding Stiles’ performance.
“Julia’s tribute to my dear friend, who I miss every single day, was amazing and stunning, and I’m so proud of her,” Krumholtz added.
He then reiterated how incredible the cast looked before joking that their appearances played a role in his absence.

“I thought the cast looked amazing. They all look so young still, and it would have been weird because I shaved what’s left of my hair,” he quipped. “Then it becomes a whole internet fodder. ‘Oh, look what happened to him.’ And oh, ‘He’s really…’ I didn’t want that, but that’s not why I wasn’t there. I would have dealt with it.”
At the end of the video he said, “Anyway, love them all. Love you all.”
Stiles confirmed that a scheduling conflict kept Krumholtz away from the ballroom when she spoke to “Entertainment Tonight” after the episode aired.

In a clip posted on Instagram, she revealed that the first person she reached out to about honoring Ledger was Gordon-Levitt. She then contacted Oleynik, whom she has “kept in touch (with) really in a nice way.” Next, Union, Pratt and Keegan agreed to show up.
“But it was like, everyone was kind of like, ‘I’ll do it if everybody else does it.’ So it just took one, you know? And it was so special to have them here,” Stiles shared.

Making sure not to leave out Krumholtz, she continued, “Oh! But wait I have to say, for the record, very important PSA: David Krumholtz, we wanted him here. He wanted to be here, but he’s working on an HBO show in New York, so there was no way he could fly to Los Angeles.”

Stiles and her partner Ezra Sosa performed a contemporary routine for their Dedication Night performance set to “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” by Frankie Valli, the song Ledger’s character sings to Stiles’ character in “10 Things I Hate About You” to convince her to go on a date with him.
Prior to the dance, Stiles opened up about how much working with Ledger, who died of an accidental overdose in 2008, meant to her. She recalled their moments on set and praised his “lust for life.”

At the end of the performance, the “10 Things I Hate About You” cast embraced one other as a photo of Stiles and Ledger from the film was displayed. Her unforgettable speech to him played through the silent ballroom.
The “DWTS” Instagram account later shared a video of the cast celebrating Stiles’ dance.

title: She Was 6 When She Played Zuzu in ‘It’s a Wonderful Life.’ Now 86, She Weighs in on New Jimmy Stewart Biopic
summary: Karolyn Grimes, once the little girl in It’s a Wonderful Life, had feedback for KJ Apa after seeming him in the new Jimmy Stewart biopic.
story: Karolyn Grimes played the part of 6-year-old Zuzu Bailey alongside Jimmy Stewart’s George Bailey in the 1946 holiday classic “It’s a Wonderful Life,” so she has firsthand knowledge of what the iconic actor was like.
When actor KJ Apa was portraying the legendary Oscar winner in the new movie, “Jimmy,” he got some direct feedback about his performance from Grimes, 86, who makes an appearance in the film.

“It’s interesting because my first time meeting her on set, she looked at me and she goes, ‘Huh. You look nothing like Jimmy Stewart,’” Apa said on TODAY Oct. 21 while laughing. “I was like, ‘Ohhhh.’”
The “Riverdale” star won her over with his portrayal of Stewart’s time as a fighter pilot in World War II as well as a few of his famous acting roles.

“Then I saw her after she watched the movie and she came and she said some really, really kind words,” Apa said. “And to have her stamp of approval meant a lot. Her and (Stewart’s daughter) Kelly, those were the only two people I was like, ‘If they’re happy with it, I can walk away really happy.’”
A sweet moment between Apa and Grimes after she first saw the film was captured in a photo Apa shared on Instagram on Oct. 9.

“I was so moved to feel the love & legacy that Jimmy left behind,” Apa wrote. “His life and work has made such an impact on so many of us and I could feel it last night. I am honored and grateful to have the opportunity to embody a man who loved his country, his family and lead through service. Jimmy Stewart was a good man. A decent man who always strove to do the right thing especially when it wasn’t easy. A simple and powerful reminder for all of us.”

Apa said he worked closely with dialect coach Eliza Simpson to embody Stewart’s inimitable voice and was busy “soaking in every part of him.” Stewart’s daughter Kelly Stewart-Harcourt gave her seal of approval to the film, which hits theaters on Nov. 6.

“But I was thrilled because the problem with somebody playing Dad ... was that you don’t want to sit there and listen to a Jimmy Stewart impersonation for two hours,” Stewart-Harcourt told Entertainment Weekly. “And Dad has such a distinctive way of speaking. It’s hard not to do an impersonation, but KJ channels him and brings him to life without doing a Jimmy Stewart impersonation. So I don’t see how they could have found anybody better.”

“Nothing makes me happier than Jimmy’s daughter Kelly loving the movie,” Apa said on TODAY. “That was the most important thing to me. People who love Jimmy, there’s so many of them. I had no idea it was that extensive how far his movies have reached.”
Apa used Stewart-Harcourt as a resource to learn more about her famous father, who died in 1997 at 89 years old.
“She shared so many stories about her father,” Apa said. “It was really special to have her involved every step of the way so that we could tell an authentic story.”

title: An Emotional ‘DWTS’ Dedication Night Ends With Shocking News
summary: It’s Dedication Night on “Dancing With the Stars,” and the 10 remaining couples are performing emotional and heartfelt routines.
story: It’s Dedication Night on “Dancing With the Stars” and it’s sure to be an emotional one.
The remaining 10 couples are performing routines honoring the special people and places in their lives during the Tuesday, Oct. 20 episode.

After last week’s elimination of fan favorites Guillermo Rodriguez and Witney Carson, the pairs will give it their all to make it another week. In a turn of events, eliminated pro Alan Bersten is filling in for Val Chmerkovskiy after being suspended for his reaction to Carrie Ann Inaba’s critique of his wife Jenna Johnson’s performance.
His absence was quickly mentioned at the top of the episode by co-host Alfonso Ribeiro, who noted, “As you can see Alan Bersten is with Jenna Dewan because Val is not with us this week.”
As the night kicked off, Ribeiro and Julianne Hough welcomed Kym Johnson as she joined Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough as a guest judge.
The first dance by Ezra Frech got the judges emotional. He performed a contemporary dedicated to his mother, who joined him on the ballroom floor.
Tatyana Ali also invited Ribeiro, who portrayed her TV brother on  “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,” to join her Viennese waltz in honor of the late James Avery.
